definition_en: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something
core_image: 胸口像被一团火点着，忍不住向前倾身去做那件事
scene: 听说球队要打决赛，整条街的人都兴奋地讨论起来。When the team reached the final, the whole street discussed it with enthusiasm.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiasm 是「热情」（第 1 个义项：强烈的兴奋与兴趣）；句意：球队打进决赛时，整条街的人都热情地讨论这件事。

senses.title: Strong excitement and interest
senses.definition: a strong feeling of eagerness and interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈的渴望与兴趣
senses.example: She spoke about the project with great enthusiasm.
senses.exampleCN: 她满腔热情地谈起这个项目。
senses.why: The Greek source describes a god within, and that inner fire becomes strong excited interest.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源描述「心中有神」，这种内心之火就变成强烈的兴奋与兴趣。

senses.title: An object of passionate interest
senses.definition: an activity or subject that someone pursues with great eagerness
senses.definitionCN: 某人满怀热忱去从事的活动或主题
senses.example: Gardening is one of her lifelong enthusiasms.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是她终身的爱好之一。
senses.why: The feeling is transferred to the thing that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这种情感被转移到产生它的事物上。

senses.title: Fervent devotion to a cause
senses.definition: intense and sometimes uncritical devotion to a belief or cause
senses.definitionCN: 对信念或事业强烈、有时缺乏批判的投入
senses.example: His early enthusiasm for the movement later cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 他早年对这场运动的狂热后来冷却了。
senses.why: The original religious intensity survives in this formal sense of devoted zeal.
senses.whyCN: 原初的宗教强度保留在这个正式的「热诚」义项中。

intro.en: Enthusiasm comes from Greek enthousiasmos, divine possession, from entheos, having a god within, built on en- and theos, god.
intro.cn: enthusiasm 来自希腊语 enthousiasmos（神灵附体），源于 entheos（心中有神），由 en- 与 theos（神）构成。

items.en: Theos means god.
items.cn: theos 意为神。

items.en: Entheos means having a god within, inspired.
items.cn: entheos 意为心中有神、受神灵启发的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession or inspired frenzy.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体、受神启的狂热。

items.en: Enthusiasmus carries the term into learned Latin.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个词带入学术拉丁语。

items.en: English adopts enthusiasm for possession by a god.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，英语用 enthusiasm 表示神灵附体。

items.en: The word now means strong excited interest in almost anything.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词表示对几乎任何事物的强烈兴趣。

note.en: Enthusiasm is a fire word, and it sits near its own family and near words for passion and zeal.
note.cn: enthusiasm 是一个「火焰」词，与自身词族以及表示激情和热忱的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who is very interested in something
in an eager and excited way
a very strong feeling or interest
the state of wanting something very much

normalIntro.en: Enthusiasm comes from Greek entheos, having a god within: the word pictures fire inside a person.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiasm 来自希腊语 entheos（心中有神）：这个词描绘人体内的一团火。

normal.en: Theos means god, so enthusiasm once meant divine possession.
normal.cn: theos 意为神，所以 enthusiasm 原指神灵附体。

normal.en: Modern enthusiasm is simply strong excitement and interest.
normal.cn: 现代的 enthusiasm 就是强烈的兴奋与兴趣。

normal.en: Enthusiasm for something is the usual pattern with a noun.
normal.cn: enthusiasm for something 是常见的名词搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is enthusiastic, and the person is an enthusiast.
normal.cn: 形容词是 enthusiastic，指人是 enthusiast。

normal.en: Compare passion: passion burns quietly, while enthusiasm shows itself openly.
normal.cn: 对比 passion：passion 安静地燃烧，enthusiasm 则外露。

abstract.en: Picture a spark catching dry grass and spreading fast.
abstract.cn: 想象火星落在干草上，迅速蔓延。

abstract.en: Imagine a child pulling a parent toward a festival tent.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子拉着父母往节日的帐篷跑。

abstract.en: Think of a room leaning forward to hear one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象整个房间的人都前倾身体听一个声音。

examples.en: She spoke about the project with great enthusiasm.
examples.cn: 她满腔热情地谈起这个项目。

examples.en: His enthusiasm for music began at school.
examples.cn: 他对音乐的热情始于学校。

examples.en: The crowd's enthusiasm lifted the players.
examples.cn: 观众的热情鼓舞了球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en-theos」——心里住着一位神，所以热情高涨；这只是词源拆解式联想，与日常读音无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（神灵附体般的激情）→ 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 英语 enthusiasm。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as divine possession, softens into religious fervor, and finally becomes the everyday fire of strong interest.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词最初指神灵附体，后淡化为宗教热诚，最终成为日常所说的强烈兴趣之火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire lit inside a person that pushes them forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：心中燃起一团火，推着人向前。

branches.en: Strong excited interest is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 强烈兴奋的兴趣，是现代日常义项。

branches.en: The thing that lights the fire becomes an enthusiasm too.
branches.cn: 点燃火焰的事物本身也被称作 enthusiasm。

branches.en: Devotion to a cause keeps the original intensity.
branches.cn: 对事业的投入保留了原初的强度。

branches.en: People feel enthusiasm, and their hobbies are their enthusiasms.
branches.cn: 人怀有热情，而爱好就是他们所热衷的事物。

branches.en: A lifelong hobby and a cause can both command devotion.
branches.cn: 终身爱好与事业都能赢得投入。

intro.en: Enthusiasm is a Greek word that reached English through Latin, and English endings form its modern family.
intro.cn: enthusiasm 是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊词，现代词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek theos means god, and entheos means having a god within; Latin enthusiasmus carries the word westward.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theos 表示神，entheos 表示心中有神；拉丁语 enthusiasmus 把这个词带向西方。

definition_en: showing strong excitement and interest
core_image: 眼睛里发亮，身体前倾，抢着把喜欢的事说给别人听
scene: 新来的志愿者一进门就热情地介绍起周末的活动安排。The new volunteer was enthusiastic about the weekend programme from the moment she arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiastic 是「热情的」（第 1 个义项：表现出强烈兴趣）；句意：新志愿者一进门就对周末的活动安排充满热情。

senses.title: Showing strong eager interest
senses.definition: showing a lot of excitement and interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物表现出大量兴奋与兴趣
senses.example: The children were enthusiastic about the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对这次旅行充满热情。
senses.why: The -ic adjective turns the inner fire of enthusiasm into a visible quality.
senses.whyCN: -ic 形容词把 enthusiasm 的内心之火变成看得见的品质。

senses.title: Eager to take part
senses.definition: very willing to join an activity or help
senses.definitionCN: 非常愿意参加活动或提供帮助
senses.example: The volunteers were enthusiastic about starting work at once.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们恨不得马上开始工作。
senses.why: Eagerness to act is enthusiasm directed at doing something.
senses.whyCN: 急于行动，就是指向做事的热情。

senses.title: Expressing warm approval
senses.definition: showing strong and warm support for a plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法表现出强烈而热烈的支持
senses.example: The plan won enthusiastic support from the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划赢得了全队的热烈支持。
senses.why: Approval becomes enthusiastic when it is expressed with the same heat as interest.
senses.whyCN: 当赞同以与兴趣同样的热度表达出来，就成了「热烈赞同」。

intro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm with the adjective ending -ic, from Greek entheos, having a god within.
intro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加形容词词尾 -ic，源于希腊语 entheos（心中有神）。

items.en: Theos means god, and entheos means inspired by a god.
items.cn: theos 意为神，entheos 意为受神启发的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession or inspired fervor.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体或受神启的热忱。

items.en: Enthusiasmus brings the noun into Latin learning.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个名词带入拉丁学术。

items.en: Enthusiasm enters English with its religious intensity.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，enthusiasm 带着宗教强度进入英语。

items.en: The ending -ic forms enthusiastic as a describing word.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，词尾 -ic 构成形容词 enthusiastic。

items.en: Enthusiastic now describes visible eagerness in any field.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enthusiastic 描述任何领域中看得见的热情。

note.en: Enthusiastic is the -ic adjective of enthusiasm, and it sits near its family and near words for eager and keen.
note.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 的 -ic 形容词，与自身词族以及表示渴望和热切的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who is very interested
wanting to do something very much

normalIntro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm turned into an adjective with -ic.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加 -ic 变成的形容词。

normal.en: Drop -ism and add -ic: the noun becomes the describing word.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ism 加上 -ic，名词就变成形容词。

normal.en: Enthusiastic about is the most common pattern.
normal.cn: enthusiastic about 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: An enthusiastic response is louder than a polite one.
normal.cn: enthusiastic response 比礼貌性的回应更热烈。

normal.en: The adverb enthusiastically adds -ally to the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 enthusiastically 在形容词后加 -ally。

normal.en: Compare keen: keen is quieter and more common in British English.
normal.cn: 对比 keen：keen 更含蓄，在英式英语中更常见。

abstract.en: Picture hands raised before the question is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没问完，手已经举起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a door thrown open for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象门被猛地拉开迎接客人。

abstract.en: Think of a face lit by a screen at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜时分被屏幕照亮的一张脸。

examples.en: The children were enthusiastic about the trip.
examples.cn: 孩子们对这次旅行充满热情。

examples.en: She gave an enthusiastic welcome to the guests.
examples.cn: 她热情地欢迎客人。

examples.en: His enthusiastic support helped the plan succeed.
examples.cn: 他的热情支持帮助计划取得成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enthusiasm + tic」——热情像小动作一样藏不住，一阵一阵往外冒；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（受神启的激情）→ 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 英语 enthusiasm ＋ -ic → enthusiastic。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes the outer signs of the inner fire: bright interest, readiness to act, and warm approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词描述内心之火的外在迹象：明亮的兴趣、随时行动的意愿，以及热烈的赞同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit face leaning forward, eager to speak or act.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张发亮的脸向前倾，急着说话或行动。

branches.en: Visible interest is the basic adjective sense.
branches.cn: 看得见的兴趣，是形容词的基本义项。

branches.en: Readiness to act turns interest into participation.
branches.cn: 随时行动的意愿把兴趣变成参与。

branches.en: Warm approval directs the same energy at a plan.
branches.cn: 热烈赞同把同样的能量指向一项计划。

branches.en: An interested person usually wants to join in.
branches.cn: 有兴趣的人通常想参与。

branches.en: Eager helpers often give loud support.
branches.cn: 热心的帮手常常给出响亮的支持。

intro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm reshaped with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加上形容词词尾 -ic 构成的。

latinIntro.en: Greek theos, god, lies behind the whole family, and the -ic ending is English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theos（神）是整个词族的根源，-ic 词尾则来自英语。

items.example: Theos is the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: theos 是这个词族的核心。

items.example: Entheos supplies the image of inner fire.
items.exampleCN: entheos 提供内心之火的画面。

items.example: Enthousiasmos is the Greek noun source.
items.exampleCN: enthousiasmos 是希腊语名词来源。

definition_zh: 全部的；整个的；完整无缺的
definition_en: whole, with no part missing or left out
core_image: 一块布从一头铺到另一头，没有一处缺口
scene: 大雪下了整整一夜，第二天整个村子都白了。Snow fell all night, and the entire village was white by morning.
sceneCN: 这里 entire 是「整个的」（第 1 个义项：完整无缺的全部）；句意：雪下了一整夜，到早晨整个村子都白了。

pos.zh: 全部的；整个的；完整无缺的

senses.title: Whole, with nothing left out
senses.definition: including every part of something, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 包含某物的每一部分，没有遗漏
senses.example: The entire class passed the test.
senses.exampleCN: 全班都通过了考试。
senses.why: The Latin root means untouched and whole, so the adjective names a thing with no part removed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「未被触碰、完整」，所以这个形容词指没有去掉任何部分的事物。

senses.title: Complete and unbroken
senses.definition: still in one piece, not damaged or divided
senses.definitionCN: 仍为一体，没有损坏或分裂
senses.example: The ancient wall is still entire after two thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 两千年后，这堵古墙依然完整。
senses.why: The original sense of untouched survives in the idea of something whole and undamaged.
senses.whyCN: 「未被触碰」的原义，保留在「完整无损」这一含义中。

senses.title: Complete in degree
senses.definition: complete or total in an abstract sense, such as trust or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在抽象意义上完全、彻底，如信任或一致
senses.example: He had the entire confidence of the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他拥有董事会的完全信任。
senses.why: Whole applied to abstract things means complete and unreserved.
senses.whyCN: 「整体」用于抽象事物，就表示完全、毫无保留。

intro.en: Entire comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成，经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Middle English entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: Modern English uses entire mainly for the whole of something.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entire 主要用于表示某事物的全部。

note.en: Entire is a wholeness word, and it sits near its family and near words for whole and complete.
note.cn: entire 是一个「完整」词，与自身词族以及表示全部和完整的词相邻。

entries.definition: to combine parts into a whole

normalIntro.en: Entire comes from Latin integer, untouched or whole, so the word pictures something with no part removed.
normalIntro.cn: entire 来自拉丁语 integer（未被触碰、完整），所以这个词描绘没有去掉任何部分的事物。

normal.en: Integer means whole, and it also gives us the mathematical integer.
normal.cn: integer 意为完整，也给我们数学中的「整数」。

normal.en: The entire day means all of it, with nothing left out.
normal.cn: the entire day 指一整天，没有遗漏。

normal.en: The adverb entirely means completely.
normal.cn: 副词 entirely 表示完全地。

normal.en: The noun entirety appears in the phrase in its entirety.
normal.cn: 名词 entirety 出现在短语 in its entirety 中。

normal.en: Compare whole: whole is plainer, while entire is slightly more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 whole：whole 更朴素，entire 稍正式。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with no corner torn away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸没有任何一角被撕掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a circle closed without the smallest gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆闭合得没有一丝缺口。

abstract.en: Think of a house lit from every window at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子的每扇窗同时亮起。

examples.en: The entire class passed the test.
examples.cn: 全班都通过了考试。

examples.en: She read the entire report in one sitting.
examples.cn: 她一口气读完了整份报告。

examples.en: The entire village came to the wedding.
examples.cn: 全村人都来参加婚礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——一条轮胎也没有漏掉，就是完整无缺的全部；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺的）→ 古法语 entier → 中古英语 entire，核心义「未被触碰、完整」。

sensesIntro.en: The word keeps the old sense of untouched wholeness, then extends it to physical completeness and finally to complete trust or agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词保留「未被触碰的完整」这一古老含义，再扩展到物理上的完好，最后用于完全的信任或一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Including every part is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 包含每一部分，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Physical soundness keeps the original untouched idea.
branches.cn: 物理上的完好保留原初「未被触碰」的意思。

branches.en: Complete trust applies wholeness to abstract things.
branches.cn: 完全的信任把「整体」用于抽象事物。

branches.en: Something whole in quantity is often also whole in condition.
branches.cn: 数量上完整的东西，状况上往往也完好。

branches.en: The whole of a thing can be given completely or trusted fully.
branches.cn: 事物的整体可以被完整给出，也可以被完全信任。

intro.en: Entire is a Latin adjective reshaped by French, and its English family grows with -ly, -ty, and -ness.
intro.cn: entire 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，英语词族由 -ly、-ty 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.exampleCN: in- 在 integer 中否定 tangere。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.
Integer is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: integer 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entier 把这个词带入法语。
entirely 表示在每一部分上。

表示状态或性质的词尾

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
items.exampleCN: entireness 是 entirety 的罕见同义词。

definition_en: completely, or only and nothing else
core_image: 一块布从头铺到尾，没有一寸遗漏
scene: 暴雨过后，整条山路都被泥水覆盖。After the storm, mud covered the mountain path entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 entirely 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：在程度或范围上毫无遗漏）；句意：暴雨过后，泥水把山路完全盖住了。

senses.title: Completely, in every part
senses.definition: in every part or to the full degree, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 在每一部分上或达到十足程度，没有任何遗漏
senses.example: I agree with you entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to entire, so it describes something done in a whole and complete way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 entire 加 -ly 构成，所以描述以完整、彻底的方式完成某事。

senses.title: Solely, and nothing else
senses.definition: used to say that something is only or wholly due to one thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事仅仅或完全由于某一原因
senses.example: The decision was entirely hers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定完全是她做的。
senses.why: If something is whole, nothing else is mixed in, so entirely can mean solely.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物是完整的，就没有别的东西掺入，因此 entirely 可以表示「仅仅」。

senses.title: Fully and without reservation
senses.definition: with complete commitment or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 带着完全的投入或赞同
senses.example: She trusted him entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全信任他。
senses.why: Complete agreement leaves no room for doubt, which gives the sense of full-hearted trust.
senses.whyCN: 完全的赞同不留怀疑余地，于是产生「全心信任」的含义。

intro.en: Entirely is the adverb of entire, which comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entirely 是 entire 的副词形式；entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: The adverb entirely means completely or solely.
items.cn: 现代英语副词 entirely 表示完全地或仅仅。

note.en: Entirely belongs to the entire family and sits close to adverbs for complete degree.
note.cn: entirely 属于 entire 词族，并与表示完全程度的副词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Entirely is simply entire plus -ly: whatever is whole is done in a whole way.
normalIntro.cn: entirely 就是 entire 加 -ly：完整的东西，就以完整的方式去做。

normal.en: Entire means whole, so entirely means in a whole way.
normal.cn: entire 意为完整，所以 entirely 表示以完整的方式。

normal.en: Not entirely sure means not completely sure.
normal.cn: not entirely sure 就是不完全确定。

normal.en: The phrase entirely up to you means completely your choice.
normal.cn: 短语 entirely up to you 表示完全由你决定。

normal.en: Entirely can also mean solely, as in entirely her fault.
normal.cn: entirely 也可表示「仅仅」，如 entirely her fault。

normal.en: Compare partly, its opposite in degree.
normal.cn: 对比 partly，它是程度上的反义词。

abstract.en: Picture a blank sheet with no edge torn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空白纸，边缘一处也没有撕破。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp lighting every corner of one room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮一个房间的每个角落。

abstract.en: Think of a full glass filled to the very brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃杯被倒到最满。

examples.en: The room was entirely empty when we arrived.
examples.cn: 我们到达时，房间完全是空的。

examples.en: Her answer was not entirely honest.
examples.cn: 她的回答并不完全诚实。

examples.en: The program is entirely free for students.
examples.cn: 这个项目对学生完全免费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——轮胎一个都没落下，整辆车都齐全；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺）→ 古法语 entier → entire ＋ -ly → entirely，核心义「完整地、完全地」。

sensesIntro.en: Entirely first means in every part, then narrows to solely, and finally describes full-hearted commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: entirely 先表示在每一部分上，再收窄为「仅仅」，最后描述毫无保留的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Completeness in every part is the main adverbial sense.
branches.cn: 每一部分都完整，是主要副词义项。

branches.en: Wholeness with nothing mixed in gives the sense of solely.
branches.cn: 完整而没有别物掺入，产生「仅仅」的含义。

branches.en: Complete agreement extends the idea to full trust.
branches.cn: 完全的赞同把这一概念扩展到全心信任。

branches.en: Doing something completely often means doing it wholeheartedly.
branches.cn: 完全地做某事，往往意味着全身心投入。

branches.en: A decision made solely by one person can be trusted entirely.
branches.cn: 完全由一个人做出的决定，也可以被完全信任。

intro.cn: entirely 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.exampleCN: in- 在 integer 中否定 tangere。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.
Integer is the direct Latin source.

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.

entirely 表示在每一部分上。

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
items.exampleCN: entireness 是 entirety 的罕见同义词。

definition_zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名
definition_en: to give someone a right, or to give a title to something
core_image: 一张写着名字的证件，让人有资格走进门内
scene: 公司规定，工作满一年的员工可以享受额外假期。The company entitles every worker with a year of service to extra holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 entitles 是 entitle 的第三人称单数，表示「使有权享受」（第 1 个义项：赋予某人权利或资格）；句意：公司让工作满一年的员工有权享受额外假期。

pos.zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名

senses.title: To give someone a right
senses.definition: to give a person the legal or moral right to have or do something
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某人拥有或做某事的法律或道义权利
senses.example: The law entitles citizens to free medical care.
senses.exampleCN: 法律使公民有权享受免费医疗。
senses.why: En- adds a sense of putting someone into a state, and title supplies the legal claim, so the verb means to grant a right.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示使人进入某种状态，title 提供法律主张的含义，所以这个动词表示授予权利。

senses.title: To give a title to a work
senses.definition: to give a name or title to a book, film, song, or other work
senses.definitionCN: 给书、电影、歌曲或其他作品起名称
senses.example: The author entitled her first novel The Long Road.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她的第一部小说命名为《长路》。
senses.why: Title also means the name of a work, so to entitle is to put a title on it.
senses.whyCN: title 也指作品的名称，因此 entitle 就是给作品加上标题。

senses.title: To give a name or label to a person
senses.definition: to give someone a particular name, label, or description
senses.definitionCN: 给某人一个特定的称呼、标签或描述
senses.example: Critics entitled him the voice of his generation.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称他为那一代人的声音。
senses.why: A title can be an honor or a label, so the verb extends from naming works to naming people.
senses.whyCN: 称号既可以是荣誉也可以是标签，所以这个动词从给作品命名扩展到称呼人。

intro.en: Entitle comes from Latin titulus, a title or label, through Old French entitler, meaning to give a title to.
intro.cn: entitle 来自拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号），经古法语 entitler（给……加标题）进入英语。

items.en: Titulus means a title, label, or inscription.
items.cn: titulus 意为标题、标签或铭文。

items.en: Intitulare means to give a title to something.
items.cn: intitulare 意为给某物加上标题。

items.en: Entitler carries the legal and naming senses.
items.cn: entitler 同时带有法律与命名的含义。

items.en: Entitle means both to name and to give a claim.
items.cn: 中古英语 entitle 既表示命名，也表示赋予权利。

items.en: Modern English keeps the right sense in be entitled to.
items.cn: 现代英语在 be entitled to 中保留「有权」的含义。

note.en: Entitle is a giving word: it gives rights or names, so its company includes title words and words for granting.
note.cn: entitle 是一个「给予」词：给予权利或名称，所以它与 title 词族及表示授予的词相邻。

entries.definition: the name of a work or a rank
having a right or a title
to give official power or permission
to give a name to something

normalIntro.en: Entitle is en- plus title: to put someone or something into a title, whether a legal claim or a name.
normalIntro.cn: entitle 是 en- 加 title：把人或事物放进一个「名分」里，既可以是法律权利，也可以是名称。

normal.en: A ticket entitles you to a seat, and the verb entitles you to a right.
normal.cn: 一张票让你有座位，动词 entitle 让你有权利。

normal.en: Be entitled to means have the right to.
normal.cn: be entitled to 表示有权享有。

normal.en: A book is entitled, and so is a film.
normal.cn: 书可以被命名，电影也可以。

normal.en: The noun entitlement names the right itself.
normal.cn: 名词 entitlement 指权利本身。

normal.en: Compare title: title is the name, entitle is the act of giving it.
normal.cn: 对比 title：title 是名称，entitle 是给予名称的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a key being placed into a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被放进一双等待的手中。

abstract.en: Imagine a label being tied to a new book.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签被系在一本新书上。

abstract.en: Think of a name written at the top of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写在页面顶端。

examples.en: This pass entitles you to enter the gallery.
examples.cn: 这张通行证使你有权进入画廊。

examples.en: She entitled her essay A Quiet Morning.
examples.cn: 她把自己的文章命名为《安静的早晨》。

examples.en: The ticket entitles each visitor to one free drink.
examples.cn: 这张票让每位参观者有权获得一杯免费饮料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + title」——给你一个「头衔」，你就有资格；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号）→ 拉丁语 intitulare（加标题）→ 古法语 entitler → 中古英语 entitle，核心义「给予名分」，引申为赋予权利。

sensesIntro.en: Entitle moves from granting a legal claim to giving a work a title, and then to giving a person a label.
sensesIntro.cn: entitle 从授予法律权利，扩展到给作品加标题，再扩展到给人加称号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document with a name on it that opens a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写有名字、可以打开一扇门的文书。

branches.en: Granting a right is the dominant legal sense.
branches.cn: 授予权利，是主要的法律义项。

branches.en: Giving a work its name keeps the original title idea.
branches.cn: 给作品命名，保留最初的「标题」概念。

branches.en: Giving a person a label extends naming to people.
branches.cn: 给人加称号，把命名扩展到人。

branches.en: Both rights and titles are things formally granted.
branches.cn: 权利与称号都是被正式授予的东西。

branches.en: A person can be legally entitled and publicly entitled.
branches.cn: 一个人可以依法有权，也可以被公开称呼。

intro.en: Entitle is built from en-, a Latin title word, and English endings for the derived forms.
intro.cn: entitle 由 en-、拉丁语 title 词根以及构成派生形式的英语词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin titulus means a title or inscription, and intitulare means to give a title.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 titulus 意为标题或铭文，intitulare 意为加上标题。

items.example: En- puts a person into a titled state.
items.exampleCN: en- 把人带入拥有名分的状态。

items.example: Titulus is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: titulus 是这个词族的词根。

items.example: Intitulare adds the Latin verb form.
items.exampleCN: intitulare 提供拉丁语动词形式。

items.example: Entitler brings the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entitler 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: to give a right or title
items.exampleCN: entitle 同时保留两种含义。

items.meaning: forming a past form or adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式或形容词的词尾

items.example: Entitled describes someone with a claim.
items.exampleCN: entitled 描述拥有权利的人。

items.example: Title is the shorter noun beside the verb.
items.exampleCN: title 是与动词并存的较短名词。

definition_zh: 入口；门口；进入；入场；使入迷；使出神
definition_en: a door or gate that you go through to enter a place; the act of entering; to fill someone with wonder so that they cannot think of anything else
core_image: 一扇敞开的门：人穿过它走进去，或被门里的景象牢牢吸住
scene: 暴雨中她终于找到博物馆侧面的那扇小门。She stood at the entrance of the museum, shaking the rain off her umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里 entrance 是「入口、门口」（第 1 个义项：进入一个地方的门或通道）；句意是她站在博物馆入口处抖落伞上的雨水。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人着迷的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「入迷；出神」
同源词形变化，义为「进入；条目」

senses.title: A door or gate by which you enter a place
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage that you go through to get into a building or place
senses.definitionCN: 进入建筑物或场地时穿过的门、大门或通道
senses.example: We waited for her at the main entrance of the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站正门口等她。
senses.why: The word comes from enter plus the noun suffix -ance, so the core image is the point where entering physically happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 enter（进入）加名词后缀 -ance 构成，核心意象就是「进入」动作实际发生的那扇门。

senses.title: The act of entering a place
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, or the right to do so
senses.definitionCN: 走进某个地方的行为，或获准进入的权利
senses.example: Entrance to the exhibition is free on Mondays.
senses.exampleCN: 展览入场周一免费。
senses.why: Because the suffix -ance turns an action into a noun, the word also names the act of entering itself, not just the doorway.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 能把动作名词化，所以 entrance 也指「进入」这个行为本身，而不仅仅是门口。

senses.title: Admission to a school or organization
senses.definition: the right or permission to join a school, university, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 加入学校、大学或组织的权利或许可
senses.example: She passed the entrance exam and entered the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过入学考试，进入了那所大学。
senses.why: Entering an institution is entering a gate in a figurative sense, so the act of entering extends to admission.
senses.whyCN: 进入一所学校就像穿过一扇比喻的门，「进入」的动作自然延伸为「录取、准入」。

senses.title: A person's first appearance before an audience
senses.definition: the moment when an actor or performer comes onto a stage
senses.definitionCN: 演员或表演者登上舞台的时刻
senses.example: The actor missed his entrance cue in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 演员在第二幕错过了登场提示。
senses.why: Stepping onto a stage is entering a space in front of an audience, so the act of entering narrows to a theatrical appearance.
senses.whyCN: 走上舞台就是当着观众「进入」一个空间，「进入」于是具体化为戏剧中的登场。

senses.title: To fill someone with great wonder
senses.definition: to fill someone with delight and wonder so that they forget everything else
senses.definitionCN: 使某人充满喜悦与惊奇，以至忘掉周围的一切
senses.example: The children were entranced by the magician's tricks.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被魔术师的戏法迷住了。
senses.why: As a verb, entrance means to make someone enter a trance-like state of wonder, shifting from doors to a spellbound mind.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，entrance 表示让人「进入」一种入迷出神的状态，语义从门转到了被迷住的心。

senses.title: To charm so deeply that one cannot look away
senses.definition: to charm or fascinate someone completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底迷住或吸引住某人
senses.example: The audience sat entranced throughout the whole performance.
senses.exampleCN: 整场演出中观众都看得入了神。
senses.why: This grows out of the trance image: fascination is a trance that holds the eyes and mind at the doorway of attention.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从「出神」意象生长出来：着迷就是一种把眼睛和心牢牢拴在注意力门口的入迷状态。

senses.title: A movement inward in dance or ritual
senses.definition: a formal movement of walking into a room or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 走进房间或仪式现场的一种正式动作
senses.example: The bride made a slow entrance as the music began.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐响起，新娘缓缓入场。
senses.why: Ceremonies turn the simple act of entering into a performed movement, extending the stage sense to formal occasions.
senses.whyCN: 仪式把「进入」这个简单动作变成一场表演，登场义由此延伸到婚礼等正式场合。

senses.title: A way in as a point of access
senses.definition: a way or means of getting access to something such as a career or a topic
senses.definitionCN: 通往事业、话题等的途径或手段
senses.example: The internship gave her an entrance into journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 这段实习为她打开了进入新闻业的大门。
senses.why: A doorway can be metaphorical, so entrance names any path that lets someone get into a field or subject.
senses.whyCN: 门可以比喻化，entrance 于是也指任何让人得以进入某个领域或话题的途径。

intro.en: Entrance as a noun comes from the verb enter plus the French-style noun suffix -ance; the verb sense meaning to fascinate was formed later from the noun, suggesting a state one enters.
intro.cn: 名词 entrance 由动词 enter 加法语式名词后缀 -ance 构成；表「使入迷」的动词用法较晚由名词引申而来，意为让人进入一种出神状态。

items.en: Latin intrare meant to go in, formed from intro (inward) and related to intra (within), the root behind English enter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为「进入」，由 intro（向内）构成，与 intra（在内）同族，是英语 enter 的词根来源。

items.en: Old French entrer carried the same meaning of going in, and the suffix -ance formed action nouns from verbs.
items.cn: 古法语 entrer 保留「进入」之义，后缀 -ance 则从动词构成表动作的名词。

items.en: English enter was borrowed from Old French in the Middle English period, and entrance appeared in the sixteenth century as the noun of entering.
items.cn: 英语 enter 在中古英语时期借自古法语；名词 entrance 于十六世纪出现，表示「进入」。

items.en: By the late sixteenth century entrance meant both the doorway and the act of entering, including admission to institutions.
items.cn: 十六世纪末，entrance 同时指门口与进入行为，并延伸出「入学、准入」之义。

items.en: The verb entrance meaning to put into a trance arose in the seventeenth century, generally explained as entrance (the noun) used as a verb, blending with the word trance.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现动词 entrance「使入迷」，一般认为是名词转作动词使用，并与 trance（出神）一词互相影响而成。

items.en: Today the noun stress falls on the first syllable for the doorway sense, while the fascinating verb is stressed on the second, keeping the two uses distinct.
items.cn: 今天名词「门口」义重音在第一个音节，动词「使入迷」义重音在第二个音节，两种用法靠重音区分。

note.en: Entrance has a look-alike cousin and a family of near-meaning words about doors, admission, and fascination.
note.cn: entrance 有一个形近词，以及一组关于门、准入与着迷的近义词。

entries.definition: the act of entering, or an item written in a list or record
entries.definitionCN: 进入的行为，或记录、清单中的一条；与 entrance 同根，但更常指进入行为和条目

entries.definition: a passage or area leading to an entrance
entries.definitionCN: 通向入口的过道或区域；entrance 的复合扩展词

entries.definition: a half-awake state in which you are not aware of your surroundings
entries.definitionCN: 半睡半醒、浑然不觉周围的状态；动词 entrance 与其义相关，但拼写相近且词源交织，trance 本身另为一词

entries.definition: the area just inside a door of a building
entries.definitionCN: 进门后紧挨着门的区域；与入口义近，多用于美式英语

entries.definition: the space where a door opens into a room or building
entries.definitionCN: 门洞；门口，侧重门框形成的开口本身

entries.definition: to interest someone so much that they cannot look away
entries.definitionCN: 深深吸引；使着迷，与动词 entrance 的「使入迷」义相近但更常用

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built on the word family and real usage of entrance.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于词族与真实用法的记忆钩子。

normal.en: enter + -ance: the suffix turns the action of entering into the noun for the doorway itself.
normal.cn: enter + -ance：后缀把「进入」这个动作名词化，就成了「入口」这个词。

normal.en: entrance exam is the gate you must pass to enter a school.
normal.cn: entrance exam（入学考试）就是进入学校前必须穿过的那扇门。

normal.en: entrance fee: money paid at the door before you go in.
normal.cn: entrance fee（入场费）是进门之前在门口付的钱。

normal.en: make an entrance: actors enter the stage, so an entrance is also an appearance.
normal.cn: make an entrance：演员「进入」舞台，所以 entrance 也有「登场」之义。

normal.en: the verb entrance is enter + trance: it makes someone enter a trance of wonder.
normal.cn: 动词 entrance 可以拆成 enter + trance：让人「进入」一种着迷出神的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a glowing doorway that pulls people toward it like a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇发光的门，像磁铁一样把人往里吸——既是入口，也让人入迷。

abstract.en: Feel the moment you step through a gate: the boundary between outside and inside.
abstract.cn: 体会跨过大门那一刻：门就是外面与里面的分界线。

abstract.en: Imagine a viewer frozen at the theater door, unable to look away from the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象观众僵在剧场门口，眼睛再也离不开舞台——被「使入迷」的样子。

examples.en: The main entrance of the hotel faces the sea.
examples.cn: 酒店的正门面向大海。

examples.en: The audience was entranced by her violin solo.
examples.cn: 观众被她的小提琴独奏迷住了。

examples.en: His perfect score guaranteed his entrance to the top university.
examples.cn: 他的满分成绩确保了他进入那所顶尖大学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因缺死」——你因太想进去而「因缺死」在门口；进去了又被舞台迷得「因缺死」挪不开眼。谐音只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 源自拉丁语 intrare（进入），由 intro（向内）派生，与 intra（在内）同族；经古法语 entrer 进入英语，动词 enter + 名词后缀 -ance 构成 entrance；「使入迷」义一般认为由名词转类而来，并与 trance（出神）相互影响。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical doorway the word fans out to the act of entering, admission, stage appearance, and finally the verb sense of charming someone into a trance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个具体的门出发，这个词扩展到进入行为、准入、舞台登场，最终落到动词义的「使人入迷出神」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway through which people or attention passes
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，人或注意力由此穿过

branches.en: The concrete door or gate of a building.
branches.cn: 建筑具体的门或大门。

branches.en: Entering widens into admission rights and entrance exams.
branches.cn: 进入行为扩展为准入权利与入学考试。

branches.en: Entering a stage becomes a performed appearance.
branches.cn: 进入舞台变成一场被观看的登场。

branches.en: The doorway turns metaphorical: a path into a career.
branches.cn: 门比喻化：成为进入某个行业的途径。

branches.en: Attention passes through the door of the mind into a trance.
branches.cn: 注意力穿过心灵之门，进入出神着迷的状态。

intro.en: Entrance is built from a French-learned verb plus a Latinate noun suffix, and its family shows how -ance names actions and states.
intro.cn: entrance 由一个借自古法语的动词加拉丁式名词后缀构成，其词族展示了 -ance 如何命名动作与状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root intr- means to go in, and it survives in a small family of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 intr- 意为「进入」，在英语中留下了一小族同源词。

items.meaningCN: 表动作、状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The entrance is on the left.

items.meaning: the act of entering or an item in a list
items.example: There is no entry in the log for today.
items.exampleCN: 日志里没有今天的记录。

items.meaning: money paid to go into a place
items.example: The entrance fee is ten yuan.

items.meaning: an exam for admission to a school
items.example: She is preparing for the entrance exam.
The patient received an intravenous drip.

items.meaning: a person whose attention turns inward
items.example: As an introvert, she recharges alone.
items.exampleCN: 作为内向者，她靠独处恢复精力。

items.meaning: to look inside one's own mind
items.example: He paused to introspect before answering.
items.exampleCN: 他停下来内省之后才回答。

items.meaning: to lead something in; to bring in for the first time
items.example: Let me introduce our new colleague.
items.exampleCN: 让我介绍一下我们的新同事。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人着迷的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「入迷」
同根名词，义为「进入；条目」

definition_zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入
definition_en: a way in, an item in a list, or a thing entered in a competition
core_image: 一扇门通向里面的房间，门边还挂着一块记录牌
scene: 博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。The side entry of the museum is open only to staff.
sceneCN: 这里 entry 是「入口」（第 1 个义项：进入的通道或门）；句意：博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。

pos.zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入

senses.title: A way in
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage through which one enters
senses.definitionCN: 供人进入的门、大门或通道
senses.example: The side entry was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 侧面的入口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: Entry first names the act of going in, and then the place where that act happens.
senses.whyCN: entry 最初指进入的动作，随后指发生这一动作的地方。

senses.title: An item in a list or record
senses.definition: a single item written in a list, diary, dictionary, or record
senses.definitionCN: 写在清单、日记、词典或记录中的单项
senses.example: He wrote a short entry in his diary.
senses.exampleCN: 他在日记里写了一条简短的记录。
senses.why: What is entered into a book becomes an entry, so the word names one recorded item.
senses.whyCN: 被写进书里的内容成为 entry，因此这个词指一条被记录的项目。

senses.title: A competition submission
senses.definition: a person or work entered in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 报名参加比赛的人或作品
senses.example: Her entry won the photography prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的参赛作品赢得了摄影奖。
senses.why: To enter a contest is to put something in, and the thing put in is the entry.
senses.whyCN: 参加比赛就是把某物投进去，被投进去的东西就是 entry。

senses.title: The act of entering
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, group, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地、加入某团体或协定的行为
senses.example: The country's entry into the trade agreement took years.
senses.exampleCN: 该国加入这项贸易协定花了好几年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply the act of going in, which still appears in formal phrases.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是进入的动作，这一含义仍出现在正式短语中。

intro.en: Entry comes from Latin intrare, to enter, through Old French entree, and it keeps both the act and the place of entering.
intro.cn: entry 来自拉丁语 intrare（进入），经古法语 entree 进入英语，同时保留「进入的动作」与「进入之处」两层含义。

items.en: Intrare means to go in or enter.
items.cn: intrare 意为走进去、进入。

items.en: Intro means within or inside.
items.cn: intro 意为在内部。

items.en: Entree names both the act and the place of entering.
items.cn: entree 同时指进入的动作和进入的地点。

items.en: Entry appears with the same double sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 entry 出现时也带有这双重含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a recorded item.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「记录条目」的含义。

note.en: Entry is a going-in word and a record word, so it sits near enter words and near words for access.
note.cn: entry 既表示「进入」，也表示「记录」，因此与 enter 词族及表示通行的词相邻。

entries.definition: a way in or the act of entering
a door or passage for entering
the right or way to enter

normalIntro.en: Entry is the noun of enter: the way in, the act of going in, or the thing you put into a list.
normalIntro.cn: entry 是 enter 的名词：进去的路、进去的动作，或你写进清单里的那一项。

normal.en: No entry means you may not go in.
normal.cn: no entry 表示禁止进入。

normal.en: A dictionary entry is one word and its explanation.
normal.cn: dictionary entry 是一个词及其解释。

normal.en: An entry form is the paper you fill in to join.
normal.cn: entry form 是报名时填写的表格。

normal.en: The plural entries covers lists and contestants alike.
normal.cn: 复数 entries 既可指多条记录，也可指多位参赛者。

normal.en: Compare entrance: entrance stresses the doorway, entry suits records and contests too.
normal.cn: 对比 entrance：entrance 强调门口，entry 还适用于记录和比赛。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow gate with a small sign beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窄门，旁边挂着一块小牌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a line written neatly in a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象笔记本上工整地写着一行字。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed box waiting on a contest table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个封好的盒子放在比赛桌上等待评审。

examples.en: The back entry leads to a small garden.
examples.cn: 后门通向一个小花园。

examples.en: Each entry in the list has a date.
examples.cn: 清单上的每一条记录都有一个日期。

examples.en: The judges praised the youngest entry.
examples.cn: 评委称赞了最年轻的参赛作品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + try」——想进去就得试一试；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entree（进入；入口）→ 中古英语 entry，核心义「进入」，引申为入口与记录条目。

sensesIntro.en: Entry begins with the act of going in, then names the place, the recorded item, and the thing submitted to a contest.
sensesIntro.cn: entry 从进入的动作开始，随后指进入之处、被记录的项目以及提交参赛的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway, with a ledger open nearby.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，旁边摊开一本登记簿。

branches.en: The doorway is the place of entering.
branches.cn: 入口是进入发生的地点。

branches.en: A recorded item is what has been entered in a book.
branches.cn: 记录条目是被写进书里的内容。

branches.en: A contest entry is what has been entered in a competition.
branches.cn: 参赛作品是被投进比赛的东西。

branches.en: The bare act of entering is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 纯粹的进入动作是最古老的含义。

branches.en: A doorway exists for the act of entering.
branches.cn: 入口正是为了进入的动作而存在。

intro.en: Entry grows from Latin intrare and Old French entree, with English relatives enter, entrance, and entrant.
intro.cn: entry 源自拉丁语 intrare 与古法语 entree，英语亲属词有 enter、entrance 与 entrant。

latinIntro.en: Latin intrare means to enter, built on intra, within.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为进入，建立在 intra（在内）之上。

items.example: Intra marks the inside of a place.
items.exampleCN: intra 标示一个地方的内部。

items.example: Intrare is the direct Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: intrare 是直接的拉丁语动词。

items.example: Entree carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entree 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: a way in or a recorded item
items.exampleCN: entry 保留两种古老含义。

items.example: Enter is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: enter 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: An entrant is someone who enters.
The ending of entry marks a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: entry 的词尾标示动作名词。

definition_en: a paper cover for a letter, or any enclosing cover
core_image: 一张纸把信折包在里面，只露出封口
scene: 她把照片放进棕色信封，写上地址。She put the photo in a brown envelope and wrote the address.
sceneCN: 这里 envelope 是「信封」（第 1 个义项：装信件或文件的纸套）；句意：她把照片装进棕色信封并写上地址。

senses.title: A paper cover for a letter
senses.definition: a flat paper container used for sending letters or papers
senses.definitionCN: 用于寄送信件或文件的扁平纸制容器
senses.example: He sealed the envelope and mailed it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信封封好并寄了出去。
senses.why: The word comes from a French verb meaning to wrap, so the paper wrapper for a letter is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「包裹」的法语动词，所以装信件的纸套是它的第一个义项。

senses.title: Any enclosing cover
senses.definition: a layer or cover that wraps something around
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从四周包起来的层或罩
senses.example: A thin envelope of dust covered the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子上覆着一层薄薄的灰尘。
senses.why: The idea of wrapping extends from paper to any surrounding layer.
senses.whyCN: 「包裹」的概念从纸张扩展到任何包围的层。

senses.title: The limit of what is accepted
senses.definition: the boundary of what is normal or possible, especially in performance
senses.definitionCN: 正常或可能范围的边界，尤指表现方面
senses.example: The test pilots pushed the envelope of speed.
senses.exampleCN: 试飞员挑战了速度的极限。
senses.why: Aircraft have a safe operating envelope, and pushing beyond it became a general image for testing limits.
senses.whyCN: 飞机有安全运行包线，越过它就成了一般意义上「挑战极限」的意象。

senses.title: A technical outer membrane
senses.definition: a membrane or outer layer enclosing a cell, virus, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 包住细胞、病毒或结构的膜或外层
senses.example: The virus is wrapped in a protein envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒外面包着一层蛋白质外膜。
senses.why: The biological sense applies the same enclosing idea at a microscopic scale.
senses.whyCN: 生物学义项把同样的包裹概念用于微观尺度。

intro.en: Envelope comes from Old French envoloper, to wrap, which goes back to Latin volvere, to roll or turn.
intro.cn: envelope 来自古法语 envoloper（包裹），其根源是拉丁语 volvere（卷、转）。

items.en: Volvere means to roll or turn around.
items.cn: volvere 意为卷动或转动。

items.en: Voloper develops the sense of wrapping.
items.cn: voloper 发展出「包裹」的含义。

items.en: Envoloper means to wrap something up.
items.cn: envoloper 意为把某物包起来。

items.en: Enveloppe names the wrapper itself.
items.cn: enveloppe 指包裹物本身。

items.en: English envelope first means a wrapper and then a letter cover.
items.cn: 英语 envelope 先指包裹物，再指信封。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical senses of limit and membrane.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「极限」与「外膜」等技术义项。

note.en: Envelope is a wrapping noun, closely tied to the verb envelop and to words for covers.
note.cn: envelope 是表示包裹的名词，与动词 envelop 以及表示覆盖的词关系紧密。

entries.definition: the act of wrapping or surrounding

normalIntro.en: Envelope is the noun of envelop: it is the thing that wraps a letter and holds it inside.
normalIntro.cn: envelope 是 envelop 的名词：它就是包住信件、把信装在里面的事物。

normal.en: A sealed envelope hides the letter until it is opened.
normal.cn: 封好的信封把信藏起来，直到被打开。

normal.en: To push the envelope is to test a limit.
normal.cn: push the envelope 就是挑战极限。

normal.en: The verb envelop means to wrap, with no final e sound.
normal.cn: 动词 envelop 意为包裹，结尾不读长音。

normal.en: A biological envelope is an outer membrane.
normal.cn: 生物学中的 envelope 是外膜。

normal.en: Compare wrapper: wrapper is general, envelope is usually paper for mail.
normal.cn: 对比 wrapper：wrapper 更泛指包装，envelope 通常指邮寄用的纸套。

abstract.en: Picture two paper flaps folding over a sealed letter.
abstract.cn: 想象两片纸翼折过来盖住一封封好的信。

abstract.en: Imagine a thin ring of dust around a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯周围有一圈薄薄的灰尘。

abstract.en: Think of a plane flying at the edge of its safe range.
abstract.cn: 想象一架飞机飞在安全范围的边缘。

examples.en: She licked the envelope and pressed it shut.
examples.cn: 她舔了舔信封，把它压紧封好。

examples.en: A soft envelope of mist lay over the field.
examples.cn: 田野上覆着一层柔和的薄雾。

examples.en: Engineers keep testing the envelope of the new design.
examples.cn: 工程师们不断测试新设计的性能极限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + velope」——把信「包」进纸里，就成信封；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（卷、转）→ 古法语 envoloper（包裹）→ enveloppe（包裹物）→ 英语 envelope，核心义「包在外面的套子」。

sensesIntro.en: Envelope starts as a paper wrapper, extends to any enclosing layer, then to a boundary of performance and a biological membrane.
sensesIntro.cn: envelope 从纸信封开始，扩展到任何包围层，再扩展到性能界限与生物外膜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paper folded around a letter, sealed on all sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸从四面折起包住一封信并封好。

branches.en: The mail cover is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 邮寄用的纸套是日常义项。

branches.en: Any enclosing layer extends the wrap idea.
branches.cn: 任何包围层都扩展了「包裹」的概念。

branches.en: The safe operating range became an image for limits.
branches.cn: 安全运行包线成为「极限」的意象。

branches.en: The biological membrane applies the outer-layer sense.
branches.cn: 生物外膜运用了「外层」义项。

branches.en: Both a letter cover and a dust layer enclose something.
branches.cn: 信封与灰尘层都把某物包在里面。

intro.en: Envelope belongs to the volvere family of wrapping words, with the verb envelop and the noun envelopment.
intro.cn: envelope 属于 volvere 这一「包裹」词族，另有动词 envelop 与名词 envelopment。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere means to roll, and involvere means to wrap around.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为卷动，involvere 意为缠绕包裹。

items.example: Involvere adds the sense of enclosing.
Envoloper is the French wrapping verb.
items.exampleCN: envoloper 是法语中表示包裹的动词。

definition_zh: 环境；周围状况；自然环境
definition_en: the natural world, or the conditions around a person or thing
core_image: 一圈空气、景物与人声把一个人围在中间
scene: 孩子们在安静的环境里读书。The children read in a quiet environment.
sceneCN: 这里 environment 是「周围状况」（第 2 个义项：影响人或事物的周边条件）；句意：孩子们在安静的环境中读书。

pos.zh: 环境；周围状况；自然环境

senses.title: The natural world
senses.definition: the air, water, land, and living things around us, especially when seen as needing protection
senses.definitionCN: 我们周围的空气、水、土地与生物，尤指需要保护的整体
senses.example: We must protect the environment for future generations.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须为子孙后代保护环境。
senses.why: The word names what surrounds us, and in modern use the whole natural world is the most prominent surround.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指围绕我们的一切，而在现代用法中，整个自然界是最突出的「周围」。

senses.title: Surrounding conditions
senses.definition: the conditions, people, and influences around a person or activity
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某人或某项活动的条件、人与影响
senses.example: A calm environment helps children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 平静的环境有助于孩子学习。
senses.why: The core sense is simply what surrounds, so it applies to homes, schools, and workplaces.
senses.whyCN: 核心含义就是「围绕之物」，因此适用于家庭、学校和工作场所。

senses.title: A computing runtime setting
senses.definition: the software and hardware setting in which a program runs
senses.definitionCN: 程序运行所依赖的软件与硬件设置
senses.example: The program runs in a virtual environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序在虚拟环境中运行。
senses.why: Technical usage treats the surrounding system as the environment of a program.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法把围绕程序的系统视为它的环境。

intro.en: Environment comes from Old French environ, around, plus the noun suffix -ment, so it literally means the state of being surrounded.
intro.cn: environment 来自古法语 environ（在周围）加名词词尾 -ment，字面意思是「被围绕的状态」。

items.en: Viron means a circle or a turn.
items.cn: viron 意为圆圈或一圈。

items.en: Environ means around or surrounding.
items.cn: environ 意为在周围、围绕。

items.en: Environnement names the surrounding conditions.
items.cn: environnement 指周围的条件。

items.en: English environment first means surroundings in general.
items.cn: 英语 environment 最初泛指周围事物。

items.en: Modern English adds the natural world and computing senses.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「自然界」与计算机义项。

note.en: Environment is a surrounding word, with a large family of adjectives and a set of near synonyms for settings.
note.cn: environment 是表示「周围」的词，拥有庞大的形容词词族，以及一组表示场景的近义词。

entries.definition: a person who works to protect nature
everything around a place or person
the place and conditions of an event
the natural home of a plant or animal

normalIntro.en: Environment is environ plus -ment: the condition of being circled by things.
normalIntro.cn: environment 是 environ 加 -ment：被事物围在中间的状态。

normal.en: Environ means around, so environment is what is around you.
normal.cn: environ 意为在周围，所以 environment 就是你周围的一切。

normal.en: The natural environment is the whole living world.
normal.cn: natural environment 指整个生命世界。

normal.en: The adjective environmental appears in environmental protection.
normal.cn: 形容词 environmental 出现在「环境保护」中。

normal.en: An environmentalist works to protect nature.
normal.cn: environmentalist 是致力于保护自然的人。

normal.en: Compare surroundings: surroundings is more local and physical.
normal.cn: 对比 surroundings：surroundings 更偏局部和物理层面。

abstract.en: Picture a soft ring of air drawn around a standing figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一个站立的人周围画着一圈柔和的气。

abstract.en: Imagine a forest folded around a small village.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林把一个小村庄环抱起来。

abstract.en: Think of a program sitting inside a glowing frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一个程序坐在发光的框架之内。

examples.en: The factory promised to protect the local environment.
examples.cn: 这家工厂承诺保护当地环境。

examples.en: A friendly environment makes new students feel welcome.
examples.cn: 友好的环境让新生感到受欢迎。

examples.en: Developers tested the app in a secure environment.
examples.cn: 开发者在安全的环境中测试了这个应用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + viron」——把你「围」在中间的一切，就是环境；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Environment starts as whatever surrounds us, then narrows to the natural world, and later extends to the setting of a program.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of air and scenery drawn around a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人周围画着一圈空气与景物。

branches.en: The natural world is the dominant public sense.
branches.cn: 自然界是主要的公共义项。

branches.en: Surrounding conditions keep the oldest spatial sense.
branches.cn: 周围条件保留最古老的空间含义。

branches.en: A runtime setting extends surroundings to software.
branches.cn: 运行环境把「周围」扩展到软件。

branches.en: The natural world is also the largest set of conditions around us.
branches.cn: 自然界也是围绕我们最大的条件集合。

branches.en: Both a classroom and a server provide conditions for activity.
branches.cn: 教室与服务器都为活动提供条件。

intro.en: Environment is environ plus -ment, and its family grows with -al, -ly, and -ist.
intro.cn: environment 由 environ 加 -ment 构成，词族再由 -al、-ly 与 -ist 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The French verb environ, to surround, goes back to viron, a circle or turn.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词 environ（围绕）可追溯到 viron（圆圈、一圈）。

scene: 这家公司因违反环保法规而被罚款。The company was fined for breaking environmental rules.
sceneCN: 这里 environmental 是「有关环境的」（第 1 个义项：与自然环境相关）；句意：这家公司因违反环保法规而被罚款。

pos.zh: 环境的；有关环境的；环保的

senses.title: Relating to the natural world
senses.definition: connected with the air, water, land, and living things that surround us
senses.definitionCN: 与我们周围的空气、水、土地和生物相关的
senses.example: The report lists the main environmental problems of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了该地区的主要环境问题。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds -al to environment, and the dominant noun sense is the natural world.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是 environment 加 -al，而该名词的主要义项是自然界。

senses.title: Relating to surrounding conditions
senses.definition: connected with the conditions that surround a person, place, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 与围绕某人、某地或某项活动的条件有关的
senses.example: Noise is a serious environmental factor in city schools.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音是城市学校中一个严重的环境因素。
senses.why: The older sense of surroundings still appears when conditions rather than nature are meant.
senses.whyCN: 当所指为条件而非自然时，仍会出现「周围环境」这一较老的含义。

senses.title: Designed to protect nature
senses.definition: designed or intended to reduce harm to the natural world
senses.definitionCN: 旨在减少对自然界的损害的
senses.example: They chose an environmental heating system for the new house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为新房选择了一套环保供暖系统。
senses.why: Because the natural world needs protection, the adjective often carries the practical sense of being eco-friendly.
senses.whyCN: 由于自然界需要保护，这个形容词常带有「对环保有利」的实用含义。

intro.en: Environmental is environment plus -al, tracing back through French environ, around, to viron, a circle.
intro.cn: environmental 是 environment 加 -al，可经法语 environ（在周围）追溯到 viron（圆圈）。

items.en: Viron means a circle or a turn.
items.cn: viron 意为圆圈或一圈。

items.en: Environ means around.
