items.en: Environnement names the surroundings.
items.cn: environnement 指周围环境。

items.en: Environment becomes the noun for surroundings.
items.cn: 英语 environment 成为表示周围环境的名词。

items.en: The adjective environmental adds -al and spreads into policy and science.
items.cn: 形容词 environmental 加 -al，并扩展到政策与科学领域。

note.en: Environmental is the adjective of environment, and it sits near other words for ecological concern.
note.cn: environmental 是 environment 的形容词，并与表示生态关切的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to living things and their homes

normalIntro.en: Environmental is environment with -al, so it describes anything belonging to the surroundings.
normalIntro.cn: environmental 是 environment 加 -al，因此描述任何属于周围环境的事物。

normal.en: Environmental protection means keeping nature safe.
normal.cn: environmental protection 指保护自然。

normal.en: Environmental law controls pollution.
normal.cn: environmental law 管控污染。

normal.en: An environmental impact is an effect on nature.
normal.cn: environmental impact 是对自然的影响。

normal.en: The adverb environmentally appears in environmentally friendly.
normal.cn: 副词 environmentally 出现在 environmentally friendly 中。

normal.en: Compare ecological: ecological is more scientific, environmental is broader.
normal.cn: 对比 ecological：ecological 更偏科学，environmental 范围更广。

abstract.en: Picture a green ring drawn around a crowded city.
abstract.cn: 想象一座拥挤的城市外围画着一圈绿色。

abstract.en: Imagine a label on a product that shows a small leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象产品标签上画着一片小叶子。

abstract.en: Think of a scientist measuring the air above a factory.
abstract.cn: 想象科学家在测量工厂上方的空气。

examples.en: Environmental damage can take decades to repair.
examples.cn: 环境破坏可能需要几十年才能修复。

examples.en: The school joined a national environmental campaign.
examples.cn: 这所学校参加了全国性的环保活动。

examples.en: They bought environmental cleaning products for the office.
examples.cn: 他们为办公室购买了环保清洁用品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「environment + al」——给「环境」加上形容词尾巴，就变成「环境的」；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 environ（在周围）＋ -ment ＋ -al → environmental，核心义「与周围环境有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Environmental begins with the natural world, still covers surrounding conditions, and often means actively friendly to nature.
sensesIntro.cn: environmental 从自然界开始，仍涵盖周围条件，并常表示积极有利于自然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of nature drawn around human activity.
core.cn: 核心意象：人类活动周围画着一圈自然。

branches.en: The natural-world sense is the main modern use.
branches.cn: 自然界的义项是现代主要用法。

branches.en: Surrounding conditions keep the older spatial sense.
branches.cn: 周围条件保留较老的空间含义。

branches.en: Being friendly to nature is a practical extension.
branches.cn: 对自然友好是实用的延伸。

branches.en: Nature is the largest set of conditions around us.
branches.cn: 自然界是围绕我们最大的条件集合。

branches.en: Protecting nature is the aim behind green choices.
branches.cn: 保护自然是环保选择背后的目标。

intro.en: Environmental stacks -al on environment, itself environ plus -ment.
intro.cn: environmental 在 environment 上叠加 -al，而 environment 本身是 environ 加 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The French verb environ, to surround, comes from viron, a circle.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词 environ（围绕）来自 viron（圆圈）。

items.example: Environmentally stresses the point of view.
items.exampleCN: environmentally 强调看问题的角度。

definition_zh: 相等的；平等的；同等的人；等于
definition_en: the same in amount, value, or status, or to be the same as something
core_image: 天平两端放着同样重的东西，横杆保持水平
scene: 两根绳子长度相同，承受的重量也一样。The two ropes are equal in length and strength.
sceneCN: 这里 equal 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上相同）；句意：两根绳子的长度和强度都相同。

senses.title: The same in amount or degree
senses.definition: having the same size, amount, value, or level as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量、价值或水平上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: Cut the cake into eight equal pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 把蛋糕切成八块大小相等的份。
senses.why: Latin aequalis means level or even, so equal first describes things that balance perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequalis 意为水平、均匀，所以 equal 首先描述完全平衡的事物。

senses.title: Having the same rights or status
senses.definition: having the same rights, opportunities, or treatment as others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他人拥有相同的权利、机会或待遇
senses.example: Every citizen deserves equal treatment under the law.
senses.exampleCN: 每位公民在法律面前都应得到平等对待。
senses.why: The idea of an even balance extends from weights and amounts to people and their rights.
senses.whyCN: 「平衡」的概念从重量和数量扩展到人及其权利。

senses.title: A person of the same rank
senses.definition: a person who has the same ability, rank, or status as another
senses.definitionCN: 能力、地位或身份与另一人相同的人
senses.example: She treats her students as her equals.
senses.exampleCN: 她把学生当作与自己平等的人。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for someone who stands on the same level.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指站在同一水平上的人。

senses.title: To be the same as
senses.definition: to be the same in amount or value as something, or to match it
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或价值上等同于某物，或与之匹敌
senses.example: Two plus three equals five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: The verb turns the balanced relation into an action of matching.
senses.whyCN: 动词把平衡关系转化为「相配、等同」的动作。

intro.en: Equal comes from Latin aequalis, uniform or even, from aequus, level or fair.
intro.cn: equal 来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀、相等），源于 aequus（平的、公平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level, even, or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均匀的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means uniform or of the same age.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的或同年的。

items.en: Equal carries the sense of even and alike.
items.cn: equal 带有「平、相同」的含义。

items.en: Equal covers amounts and the rights of people.
items.cn: 中古英语 equal 涵盖数量与人的权利。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun for a person of the same rank.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示同等之人的名词用法。

note.en: Equal is a balance word with a large family and a set of near words for sameness.
note.cn: equal 是表示「平衡」的词，拥有庞大词族，并与表示相同的一组词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Equal comes from a level root: two sides of a scale sitting perfectly even.
normalIntro.cn: equal 来自「水平」的词根：天平两边完全齐平。

normal.en: Equal parts means every part is the same size.
normal.cn: equal parts 指每一份大小相同。

normal.en: Equal rights means the same rights for everyone.
normal.cn: equal rights 指人人拥有相同权利。

normal.en: The verb equals appears in arithmetic.
normal.cn: 动词 equals 出现在算术中。

normal.en: Equality is the noun for the equal state.
normal.cn: equality 是表示平等状态的名词。

normal.en: Compare identical: identical is stricter, equal allows different forms of the same value.
normal.cn: 对比 identical：identical 更严格，equal 允许同一价值的不同形式。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with two identical weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平两端放着相同的砝码。

abstract.en: Imagine eight cake slices cut by a careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手仔细切出八块相同的蛋糕。

abstract.en: Think of two runners crossing a line at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者同时冲过终点线。

examples.en: The two teams finished with equal scores.
examples.cn: 两支队伍最终得分相同。

examples.en: The law promises equal pay for equal work.
examples.cn: 法律承诺同工同酬。

examples.en: One kilometer equals a thousand meters.
examples.cn: 一公里等于一千米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + qual」——两边一样平，就是相等；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的、公平的）→ aequalis（均匀的）→ 古法语 equal → 英语 equal，核心义「两端齐平、彼此相同」。

sensesIntro.en: Equal starts with even amounts, extends to fair treatment, then to a person of the same standing, and finally to the verb of matching.
sensesIntro.cn: equal 从数量相等开始，扩展到公平对待，再指地位相同的人，最后成为表示「等于」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale perfectly level on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两边完全水平。

branches.en: Even amount is the basic measurable sense.
branches.cn: 数量相等是基本的可测量义项。

branches.en: Fair treatment extends balance to rights.
branches.cn: 公平对待把平衡扩展到权利。

branches.en: A peer is a person on the same level.
branches.cn: 同等之人是站在同一水平上的人。

branches.en: The verb states that two things match.
branches.cn: 动词陈述两事物彼此相等。

branches.en: Equal shares and equal rights both rest on the same balance.
branches.cn: 均分与平权都建立在同一种平衡之上。

intro.en: Equal is a Latin fairness word, and English builds equality, equally, and equate around it.
intro.cn: equal 是拉丁语中表示公平的词，英语围绕它构成 equality、equally 与 equate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level and fair, and aequalis means even or uniform.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的、公平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

items.example: Equally means in the same measure.

items.exampleCN: un- 在 unequal 中否定 equal。

definition_en: in an equal way, or to the same degree
core_image: 两杯水被倒到完全相同的高度
scene: 把奖金平均分给四个孩子。Divide the prize money equally among the four children.
sceneCN: 这里 equally 是「均等地」（第 1 个义项：以相同的份额或数量）；句意：把奖金平均分给四个孩子。

senses.title: In equal shares
senses.definition: in the same amount or share for each person or part
senses.definitionCN: 给每个人或每一部分相同的数量或份额
senses.example: The money was shared equally between the two sisters.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔钱在两姐妹之间平均分配。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to equal, so it describes an action done in an even way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 equal 加 -ly 构成，描述以均衡方式完成的动作。

senses.title: To the same degree
senses.definition: to the same degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 达到相同的程度或范围
senses.example: Both plans are equally risky.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案的风险同样大。
senses.why: The balance sense extends from shares to degrees of a quality.
senses.whyCN: 「份额均衡」的概念扩展到某种品质的程度。

senses.title: Used to add a matching point
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to add a point of the same weight
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，补充一个分量相同的观点
senses.example: Equally, we must consider the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 同样，我们也必须考虑成本。
senses.why: If two points weigh the same, the second can be introduced as equally important.
senses.whyCN: 如果两个观点分量相同，第二个就可以作为同样重要的一点引出。

intro.en: Equally is equal plus -ly, from Latin aequalis, even, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equally 是 equal 加 -ly，来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀的）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means even or equal.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的、相等的。

items.en: Equal enters English as an adjective.
items.cn: equal 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly forms the adverb equally.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 equally。

items.en: Equally also introduces a second point of the same weight.
items.cn: 现代英语中，equally 也用于引出第二个同等分量的观点。

note.en: Equally is the adverb of equal, near its family and near adverbs for sameness.
note.cn: equally 是 equal 的副词，与自身词族以及表示相同的副词相邻。

entries.definition: in an even or balanced way

normalIntro.en: Equally is equal plus -ly: whatever is equal is done or measured in an equal way.
normalIntro.cn: equally 是 equal 加 -ly：相等的东西，就以相等的方式去做或衡量。

normal.en: Divide equally means give everyone the same share.
normal.cn: divide equally 指给每个人相同的一份。

normal.en: Equally important means just as important.
normal.cn: equally important 表示同样重要。

normal.en: Equally spaced dots sit the same distance apart.
normal.cn: equally spaced 的点彼此距离相同。

normal.en: Equally at the start of a sentence adds a matching point.
normal.cn: equally 放在句首，补充一个对等的观点。

normal.en: Compare evenly: evenly stresses smooth distribution, equally stresses sameness.
normal.cn: 对比 evenly：evenly 强调分布平滑，equally 强调相同。

abstract.en: Picture two glasses filled to exactly the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象两只杯子被倒到完全相同的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a row of trees planted at identical gaps.
abstract.cn: 想象一排树以相同间距种下。

abstract.en: Think of two weights resting level on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两个砝码在天平上保持水平。

examples.en: The estate was divided equally among the three children.
examples.cn: 遗产在三个孩子之间平均分配。

examples.en: Both candidates are equally qualified for the job.
examples.cn: 两位候选人都同样胜任这份工作。

examples.en: Equally, we should ask who pays for the repairs.
examples.cn: 同样，我们也应该问清谁来支付维修费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal + ly」——用「相等」的方式去做，就是同样地；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的）→ aequalis（相等的）→ 英语 equal ＋ -ly → equally，核心义「以相同的方式或程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Equally starts with equal shares, extends to equal degrees, and is then used to add a point of the same weight.
sensesIntro.cn: equally 从均分开始，扩展到相同程度，随后用于补充同等分量的观点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two containers filled to the same level.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个容器被装到同一高度。

branches.en: Equal shares are the basic distributive sense.
branches.cn: 均分是基本的分配义项。

branches.en: Equal degree extends balance to qualities.
branches.cn: 同等程度把平衡扩展到品质。

branches.en: Adding a matching point uses equal weight in argument.
branches.cn: 补充对等观点，是在论证中使用同等分量。

branches.en: A fair share and an equal degree both rest on the same measure.
branches.cn: 公平份额与相同程度都建立在同一尺度上。

branches.en: Two equally strong points can both be introduced with equally.
branches.cn: 两个同样有力的观点都可以用 equally 引出。

intro.en: Equally is a Latin balance adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: equally 是拉丁语「平衡」形容词加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, and aequalis means even.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

items.example: Equally means by the same measure.

definition_en: the tools, machines, or gear needed for a particular purpose
core_image: 一堆工具整齐摆开，随时可以带上出发
scene: 登山前，队员检查了所有装备。Before the climb, the team checked all their equipment.
sceneCN: 这里 equipment 是「装备」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的所需的工具和器材）；句意：登山前，队员检查了所有装备。

senses.title: Tools and machines for a purpose
senses.definition: the set of tools or machines used for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的整套工具或机器
senses.example: The lab bought new equipment for the students.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为学生购买了新设备。
senses.why: The noun adds -ment to equip, naming all the things supplied rather than the act of supplying.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 equip 加 -ment 构成，指被配备的全部物品，而不是配备的动作。

senses.title: Special gear for an activity
senses.definition: the clothing or gear needed for a sport, job, or journey
senses.definitionCN: 运动、工作或旅行所需的服装或装备
senses.example: Climbing equipment must be checked before every trip.
senses.exampleCN: 每次出行前都必须检查登山装备。
senses.why: Equipment can be personal gear as well as shared machines.
senses.whyCN: equipment 既可以是共用机器，也可以是个人装备。

senses.title: The act of fitting out
senses.definition: the process of supplying a person or place with what is needed, used in formal contexts
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需之物的过程，用于正式语境
senses.example: The equipment of the new hospital took a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 新医院的设备配置花了整整一年。
senses.why: The suffix -ment can name an action as well as its result, which keeps the older process sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ment 既可指动作也可指结果，因此保留了较老的「过程」含义。

intro.en: Equipment is equip plus -ment, from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship.
intro.cn: equipment 是 equip 加 -ment，源自法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资）。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备。

items.en: Equip enters English as a verb.
items.cn: equip 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ment forms the noun equipment.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 构成名词 equipment。

items.en: Equipment covers tools for work, sport, and medicine.
items.cn: 现代英语中，equipment 涵盖工作、运动和医疗器材。

note.en: Equipment is the noun of equip, close to its verb and adjective and to words for gear.
note.cn: equipment 是 equip 的名词，与它的动词、形容词形式以及表示「装备」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a set of equipment or a carriage
the equipment needed for an activity
a set of equipment for a purpose

normalIntro.en: Equipment is what equip supplies: the whole set of tools and gear.
normalIntro.cn: equipment 就是 equip 提供的东西：整套工具与装备。

normal.en: Equipment is uncountable, so say a piece of equipment.
normal.cn: equipment 不可数，所以说 a piece of equipment。

normal.en: Safety equipment protects workers.
normal.cn: safety equipment 保护工人。

normal.en: Medical equipment must be kept clean.
normal.cn: medical equipment 必须保持清洁。

normal.en: Heavy equipment moves earth and stone.
normal.cn: heavy equipment 用来移动土石。

normal.en: Compare gear: gear is more informal, equipment is broader and formal.
normal.cn: 对比 gear：gear 更口语，equipment 更宽泛正式。

abstract.en: Picture a neat row of tools laid out before a job.
abstract.cn: 想象干活前整齐摆开的一排工具。

abstract.en: Imagine a climber counting ropes and clips by a tent.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在帐篷旁清点绳索和锁扣。

abstract.en: Think of a hospital room filled with humming machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一间充满机器低鸣的医院病房。

examples.en: All equipment must be stored in a dry room.
examples.cn: 所有设备都必须存放在干燥的房间里。

examples.en: She packed her camera equipment into two bags.
examples.cn: 她把摄影器材装进了两个包。

examples.en: The school spent a large sum on sports equipment.
examples.cn: 学校在体育器材上花了一大笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equip + ment」——被「配齐」的那些东西，就是设备；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esquiper（为船只配备）→ 英语 equip（装备）＋ -ment → equipment，核心义「被配备起来的一整套用具」。

sensesIntro.en: Equipment first means the tools supplied, then personal gear, and in formal use the process of fitting out.
sensesIntro.cn: equipment 先指被提供的工具，再指个人装备，在正式用法中还指配置过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full set of tools laid out and ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整套工具摆放齐全待用。

branches.en: The tool set is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 整套工具是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Personal gear is a narrower use.
branches.cn: 个人装备是较窄的用法。

branches.en: Fitting out keeps the older process sense.
branches.cn: 配置过程保留较老的过程含义。

branches.en: Both a lab machine and a climbing rope are supplied gear.
branches.cn: 实验室机器与登山绳都是被配备的装备。

branches.en: The equipment of a place is the result of equipping it.
branches.cn: 一个场所的设备是配置过程的结果。

intro.en: Equipment is equip with -ment, and it shares the fitting-out root with the verb.
intro.cn: equipment 是 equip 加 -ment，与动词共享「配备」词根。

latinIntro.en: Old French esquiper means to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic ship word.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 esquiper 意为为船只配备，可能来自日耳曼语表示船的单词。

items.example: Gear is the informal near word.

definition_en: equal in value, meaning, or effect, or something that matches another
core_image: 两枚不同的硬币放在天平上，重量正好相同
scene: 一英里大约相当于一点六公里。One mile is roughly equivalent to one point six kilometers.
sceneCN: 这里 equivalent 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在价值、数量或意义上相同）；句意：一英里大约等于一点六公里。

senses.title: Equal in value or amount
senses.definition: having the same value, amount, or meaning as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在价值、数量或意义上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: A dollar is not equivalent to a euro.
senses.exampleCN: 一美元并不等于一欧元。
senses.why: Latin aequus means equal and valere means be worth, so equivalent literally means worth the same.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequus 意为相等，valere 意为值，因此 equivalent 字面意思就是「价值相同」。

senses.title: Equal in effect or role
senses.definition: having the same result, function, or force as something else
senses.definitionCN: 产生相同结果、功能或效力的
senses.example: Silence was equivalent to agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默等同于同意。
senses.why: If two things are worth the same, they can stand in for each other in effect.
senses.whyCN: 如果两物价值相同，它们在效果上就可以互相替代。

senses.title: A matching thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that has the same value or role as another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或物具有相同价值或角色的人或物
senses.example: This word has no exact equivalent in English.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在英语中没有完全对应的说法。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the matching item itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指与之匹配的事物本身。

intro.en: Equivalent joins Latin aequus, equal, and valere, to be worth, so it means having equal worth.
intro.cn: equivalent 结合拉丁语 aequus（相等的）与 valere（值），意为具有相同的价值。

items.en: Aequus means equal or level.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等的、平的。

items.en: Valere means to be worth or be strong.
items.cn: valere 意为值、有力量。

items.en: Aequivalere means to be worth the same.
items.cn: aequivalere 意为价值相等。

items.en: Aequivalentem is the present participle form.
items.cn: aequivalentem 是现在分词形式。

items.en: Équivalent carries the word into French.
items.cn: équivalent 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Modern English uses equivalent as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 现代英语中 equivalent 兼作形容词与名词。

note.en: Equivalent is a worth-matching word, close to its family and to words for comparability.
note.cn: equivalent 是表示「价值相配」的词，与自身词族以及表示可比性的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being equal in value
open to more than one meaning
a person or thing matching another

normalIntro.en: Equivalent is equal plus worth: two unlike things can still balance.
normalIntro.cn: equivalent 是「相等」加「价值」：两个不同的东西也可以彼此平衡。

normal.en: Equivalent to means equal in value or effect.
normal.cn: equivalent to 表示在价值或效果上等于。

normal.en: A silent answer can be equivalent to a yes.
normal.cn: 沉默的回答可能等同于同意。

normal.en: The noun equivalence names the equal state.
normal.cn: 名词 equivalence 指相等的状态。

normal.en: No exact equivalent means there is no perfect match.
normal.cn: no exact equivalent 表示没有完全对应的说法。

normal.en: Compare tantamount: tantamount is mostly about effect, equivalent is broader.
normal.cn: 对比 tantamount：tantamount 多指效果，equivalent 范围更广。

abstract.en: Picture two different coins balancing on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚不同的硬币在天平上保持平衡。

abstract.en: Imagine a translator finding a matching phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象译者找到一个对应的说法。

abstract.en: Think of two roads that lead to the same town.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路通向同一座城镇。

examples.en: Ten dimes are equivalent to one dollar.
examples.cn: 十枚十分硬币等于一美元。

examples.en: For him, losing the match was equivalent to failure.
examples.cn: 对他来说，输掉比赛等同于失败。

examples.en: The Italian word has no equivalent in my language.
examples.cn: 这个意大利语词在我的语言里没有对应词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equi + valent」——两边「价值相等」，就是等值；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（相等的）＋ valere（值）→ aequivalere（价值相等）→ 法语 équivalent → 英语 equivalent，核心义「价值或作用相等」。

sensesIntro.en: Equivalent begins with equal value, extends to equal effect, and then names the matching thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: equivalent 从价值相等开始，扩展到效果相同，再指与之匹配的事物本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two different coins balancing on one scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚不同的硬币在天平上平衡。

branches.en: Equal value is the literal core sense.
branches.cn: 价值相等是字面核心义项。

branches.en: Equal effect extends worth to results.
branches.cn: 效果相同把价值扩展到结果。

branches.en: The matching thing is the noun use.
branches.cn: 匹配之物是名词用法。

branches.en: Things of equal value often have equal effect.
branches.cn: 价值相等的事物往往效果也相同。

branches.en: A counterpart is the thing that carries equal value.
branches.cn: 对应物就是承载同等价值的事物。

intro.en: Equivalent combines a Latin equal root with a Latin worth root, plus English noun and adverb endings.
intro.cn: equivalent 结合拉丁语「相等」词根与「价值」词根，并加上英语名词和副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means equal and valere means to be worth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为相等，valere 意为值。

items.exampleCN: equivalent 保留结合后的含义。

definition_en: a long period of history with a particular character
core_image: 一条长河被刻上标记，分成一段段可命名的时期
scene: 铁路的修建开启了这个地区的新时代。The railway opened a new era for the region.
sceneCN: 这里 era 是「时代」（第 1 个义项：具有某种特征的一段长时期）；句意：铁路的修建为这个地区开启了新时代。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a long period of history marked by particular events, ideas, or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 以特定事件、思想或状况为标志的一段长历史时期
senses.example: The invention of printing began a new era.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术的发明开启了一个新时代。
senses.why: The word first meant a system of counting years, so it naturally names a marked stretch of history.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指纪年的体系，因此自然指一段被标记的历史时期。

senses.title: A notable period in a life
senses.definition: a period in a person's life associated with a particular activity or mood
senses.definitionCN: 与某种活动或情绪相关的一段个人生活时期
senses.example: Her teaching era lasted twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教学生涯持续了二十年。
senses.why: A historical era and a personal era are both bounded periods with a character.
senses.whyCN: 历史时代与个人时期都是具有某种特征的有界时期。

senses.title: A geological era
senses.definition: a major division of geological time, longer than a period
senses.definitionCN: 地质时间的主要划分，比「纪」更长
senses.example: Dinosaurs lived in the Mesozoic era.
senses.exampleCN: 恐龙生活在中生代。
senses.why: Geology borrows the general word for a very long, clearly divided span of time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用这个一般词，指极长且有明确划分的时间跨度。

intro.en: Era comes from Late Latin aera, a system of counting years, probably from Latin aes, bronze or money, whose plural is aera.
intro.cn: era 来自晚期拉丁语 aera（纪年体系），可能源于拉丁语 aes（青铜、钱币），其复数为 aera。

items.en: Aes means bronze or money.
items.cn: aes 意为青铜或钱币。

items.en: Aera is the plural of aes.
items.cn: aera 是 aes 的复数。

items.en: Aera means a system of counting years.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aera 指纪年体系。

items.en: Era carries the dating sense into Romance languages.
items.cn: era 把纪年含义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Modern English broadens era to any notable period.
items.cn: 现代英语把 era 扩展到任何显著时期。

note.en: Era is a period word, with look-alike forms and near words for long spans of time.
note.cn: era 是表示「时期」的词，拥有形近形式以及与长时间跨度相邻的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语 aes 的复数

entries.definition: a period marked by a major change

normalIntro.en: Era is a marked stretch of time: historians draw a line and give the years a name.
normalIntro.cn: era 是一段被标记的时间：历史学家画一条线，再给这些年岁一个名字。

normal.en: A new era begins when something important changes.
normal.cn: 当重要的事物发生变化，新时代就开始了。

normal.en: The digital era is the age of computers and networks.
normal.cn: digital era 是计算机与网络的时代。

normal.en: The plural eras covers several named periods.
normal.cn: 复数 eras 指多个被命名的时期。

normal.en: A geologic era is longer than a period.
normal.cn: 地质年代比「纪」更长。

normal.en: Compare epoch: an epoch is shorter and marked by a sharp change.
normal.cn: 对比 epoch：epoch 更短，以剧烈变化为标志。

abstract.en: Picture a long river with stones marking each stretch.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长河，用石头标出每一段。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar page turning into a bright new color.
abstract.cn: 想象日历翻到崭新明亮的一页。

abstract.en: Think of layers of rock holding the bones of ancient animals.
abstract.cn: 想象岩层中藏着古代动物的骨骼。

examples.en: The internet changed the era of communication.
examples.cn: 互联网改变了通信的时代。

examples.en: Her acting era ended when she moved abroad.
examples.cn: 她移居国外后，演艺时期结束了。

examples.en: The Mesozoic era is famous for its dinosaurs.
examples.cn: 中生代以恐龙闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「era」——像日历上画出的一个「段」，就是时代；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aes（青铜、钱币，复数 aera）→ 晚期拉丁语 aera（纪年体系）→ 英语 era，核心义「被标记的一段长时间」。

sensesIntro.en: Era moves from a dating system to a historical age, then to a personal period, and finally to a geological division.
sensesIntro.cn: era 从纪年体系转为历史时代，再指个人时期，最后指地质年代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long timeline cut into named stretches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长时间线被切成有名称的段落。

branches.en: A historical period is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 历史时期是现代主要义项。

branches.en: A personal period applies the same span to one life.
branches.cn: 个人时期把同样的跨度用于一生。

branches.en: A geological era is the longest technical use.
branches.cn: 地质年代是最长的技术用法。

branches.en: A person can define an era and also have an era of their own.
branches.cn: 一个人可以定义一个时代，也可以拥有自己的时期。

branches.en: Both history and geology divide time into named eras.
branches.cn: 历史学与地质学都把时间划分为有名称的时代。

intro.en: Era is a short Latin-derived noun whose English family grows mainly through compounds.
intro.cn: era 是源自拉丁语的短名词，其英语词族主要通过复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin aes means bronze or money, and its plural aera leads to the dating sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aes 意为青铜或钱币，其复数 aera 引出纪年含义。

items.example: Aes is the older Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: aes 是较早的拉丁语名词。

items.example: Aera becomes the base of era.
items.exampleCN: aera 成为 era 的基础。
era 保留「计数时间」的含义。

items.example: Epoch is a near period word.
Age is the plainer near word.
items.exampleCN: age 是更朴素的近义词。

definition_en: a mistake, or the state of being wrong
core_image: 一支箭偏出靶心，落在旁边的空处
scene: 表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。A small error in the table made the total wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 error 是「错误」（第 1 个义项：做错或写错的地方）；句意：表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。

senses.title: A mistake
senses.definition: something done or written wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 做错或写错的事情
senses.example: She spotted an error in the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现第一行有一个错误。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a wandering, so an error is a step that has strayed from the right way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词意为「游荡」，所以错误就是偏离正路的一步。

senses.title: The state of being wrong
senses.definition: the condition of holding a wrong belief or being mistaken
senses.definitionCN: 持有错误看法或弄错的状态
senses.example: I was in error about the meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 我把会议时间弄错了。
senses.why: The word can name not only the mistake but the condition of being mistaken.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅指错误本身，也可以指弄错的状态。

senses.title: A measured deviation
senses.definition: a difference between a measured or calculated value and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算值与真实值之间的差异
senses.example: The experiment allows a small margin of error.
senses.exampleCN: 这项实验允许有一个小的误差范围。
senses.why: Scientific use turns the general mistake into a measurable deviation.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法把一般性的错误转化为可测量的偏差。

intro.en: Error comes from Latin error, a wandering or mistake, from errare, to wander.
intro.cn: error 来自拉丁语 error（游荡、错误），源于 errare（漫游）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or go astray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Errur carries the word into French.
items.cn: errur 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Error names a mistake in English.
items.cn: 中古英语 error 指错误。

items.en: Modern English adds scientific and computing errors.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了科学误差与计算机错误。

note.en: Error is the noun of straying, close to err, erroneous, and to ordinary mistake words.
note.cn: error 是表示「走偏」的名词，与 err、erroneous 以及普通的「错误」词相邻。

entries.definition: a defect or responsibility for wrong

normalIntro.en: Error is a wandering step: the mind or hand leaves the straight road for a moment.
normalIntro.cn: error 是走偏的一步：头脑或手在一瞬间离开了直路。

normal.en: To make an error is to get something wrong.
normal.cn: make an error 就是把某事弄错。

normal.en: Human error causes many accidents.
normal.cn: 人为失误造成许多事故。

normal.en: An error message tells you the program failed.
normal.cn: error message 告诉你程序出错了。

normal.en: In error means by mistake.
normal.cn: in error 表示错误地。

normal.en: Compare mistake: mistake is everyday, error is slightly more formal and technical.
normal.cn: 对比 mistake：mistake 更日常，error 稍正式且更技术化。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow landing just beside the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭落在靶心旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine a pen slipping on a single letter.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖在一个字母上滑了一下。

abstract.en: Think of a clock running a few seconds fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟快了几秒钟。

examples.en: The report contains several spelling errors.
examples.cn: 报告里有几处拼写错误。

examples.en: He sent the parcel to the wrong address in error.
examples.cn: 他误把包裹寄到了错误的地址。

examples.en: Scientists try to reduce the margin of error.
examples.cn: 科学家努力缩小误差范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「err + or」——走「偏」了，就是犯错；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（游荡；错误）→ 古法语 errur → 英语 error，核心义「偏离正途」。

sensesIntro.en: Error first means a wrong act or word, then the state of being mistaken, and finally a measurable deviation.
sensesIntro.cn: error 先指做错的事或写错的地方，再指弄错的状态，最后指可测量的误差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow that lands beside the target.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭落在靶心旁边。

branches.en: A concrete mistake is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 具体的错误是日常义项。

branches.en: Being mistaken is the state sense.
branches.cn: 弄错的状态是状态义项。

branches.en: A measured deviation is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 测量偏差是技术义项。

branches.en: A person in error often makes a visible mistake.
branches.cn: 处于错误中的人往往会犯下可见的错误。

branches.en: Both a slip and a margin of error are deviations from the true value.
branches.cn: 小失误与误差范围都是对真实值的偏离。

intro.en: Error is a Latin wandering noun, with English err, erroneous, and errorless built around it.
intro.cn: error 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的名词，英语围绕它构成 err、erroneous 与 errorless。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

items.example: Err is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: err 是简短的英语动词。

definition_en: to get away from a place or a dangerous situation
core_image: 一个人从紧锁的房间里找到出口，冲了出去
scene: 火警响起时，大家迅速从后门逃离了大楼。When the fire alarm rang, everyone escaped from the building through the back door.
sceneCN: 这里 escape 是「逃离」（第 1 个义项：从危险的地方脱身）；句意：火警响起时，大家迅速从后门逃离了大楼。

senses.title: Get away from a place
senses.definition: to get out of a place where you are held or trapped
senses.definitionCN: 从被关押或困住的地方脱身
senses.example: The bird escaped from its cage.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟从笼子里逃了出去。
senses.why: The Latin source means to get out of a cloak, so escaping is slipping free from what holds you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为从斗篷中脱出，因此逃跑就是从束缚中滑脱。

senses.title: Avoid something bad
senses.definition: to avoid danger, punishment or an unpleasant experience
senses.definitionCN: 避开危险、惩罚或不愉快的经历
senses.example: They escaped injury in the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在撞车事故中幸免受伤。
senses.why: Slipping free can also mean never being caught by harm.
senses.whyCN: 滑脱出来也可以指始终没有被伤害抓住。

senses.title: Leak out
senses.definition: to come out of a container without being intended to
senses.definitionCN: 意外地从容器中出来
senses.example: Gas escaped through a small crack.
senses.exampleCN: 气体从一道小裂缝中泄漏出来。
senses.why: Anything that slips out of its proper place escapes.
senses.whyCN: 任何从应在之处滑出的东西，都算 escape。

intro.en: Escape comes from Old French escaper, from Vulgar Latin excappare, to get out of one's cloak.
intro.cn: escape 源自通俗拉丁语 excappare（从斗篷中脱出），经古法语 escaper 传入英语。

items.en: Cappa means a cloak.
items.cn: cappa 意为斗篷。

items.en: Excappare means to slip out of a cloak.
items.cn: excappare 意为从斗篷中滑脱。

items.en: Escaper means to get away.
items.cn: escaper 意为逃脱。

items.en: Escape covers leaving a place and avoiding harm.
items.cn: escape 兼指离开某处与避开伤害。

items.en: It also describes gas or liquid leaking out.
items.cn: 它也描述气体或液体泄漏。

note.en: Escape is close to flee and get away, and has a noun form with the same spelling.
note.cn: escape 与逃跑、脱身相近，并有名动同形的名词用法。

normalIntro.en: Escape pictures slipping out of a cloak: the danger grabs only cloth.
normalIntro.cn: escape 像从斗篷里滑出去：危险只抓住了衣服。

normal.en: Escape from a place means get out of it.
normal.cn: escape from a place 意为从某地逃出。

normal.en: A narrow escape means you were almost caught.
normal.cn: a narrow escape 意为险些被抓住。

normal.en: Escape attention means nobody noticed.
normal.cn: escape attention 意为没有引起注意。

normal.en: Gas can escape from a crack.
normal.cn: 气体可以从裂缝中泄漏。

normal.en: Compare flee: flee stresses running, escape stresses getting free.
normal.cn: 对比 flee：flee 强调奔跑，escape 强调脱身。

abstract.en: Picture a door found in a wall that seemed solid.
abstract.cn: 想象在一堵看似实心的墙上找到一扇门。

abstract.en: Imagine a fish slipping through a hole in a net.
abstract.cn: 想象一条鱼从网洞里滑走。

abstract.en: Think of a hand opening to let a bird fly free.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手张开，让鸟飞走。

examples.en: Two prisoners escaped during the night.
examples.cn: 两名囚犯在夜里逃跑了。

examples.en: She escaped the boring party early.
examples.cn: 她早早地逃离了那个无聊的聚会。

examples.en: Steam escaped from the kettle with a whistle.
examples.cn: 蒸汽带着哨声从水壶里冒出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「es（出）＋ cape（斗篷）」——从斗篷里钻出去，就是逃跑脱身；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 通俗拉丁语 ex-（出）＋ cappa（斗篷）→ excappare（从斗篷中脱出）→ 古法语 escaper → escape，核心义「从束缚中滑脱」。

sensesIntro.en: Escape first means leave a trap, then avoid harm, and finally slip out of a container.
sensesIntro.cn: escape 先指离开困境，再指避开伤害，最后指从容器中漏出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person slipping free and running through an open door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人挣脱束缚，从敞开的门跑出去。

branches.en: Getting out of a place is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 从某处脱身是基本义。

branches.en: Avoiding danger is escaping in a wider sense.
branches.cn: 避开危险是更宽泛意义上的逃脱。

branches.en: Gas or liquid escapes by leaking out.
branches.cn: 气体或液体通过泄漏逃出。

branches.en: Leaving the scene often means avoiding harm.
branches.cn: 离开现场往往意味着避开伤害。

branches.en: Both a prisoner and a gas can slip out.
branches.cn: 囚犯和气体都能「滑出去」。

intro.en: Escape is built on Latin cappa, a cloak, with ex- meaning out.
intro.cn: escape 建立在拉丁语 cappa（斗篷）之上，ex- 意为出。

latinIntro.en: Vulgar Latin excappare means to get out of one's cloak.
latinIntro.cn: 通俗拉丁语 excappare 意为从斗篷中脱出。

items.meaning: to slip out of a cloak

items.example: Old French escaper carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 escaper 传递了该词。

latinEntries.meaning: to slip out of a cloak

definition_en: more than usual, or for one particular purpose
core_image: 一群人中有一张脸被聚光灯单独照亮
scene: 考前复习时，他尤其重视错题，反复看那些容易出错的题。When reviewing before the exam, he paid special attention to mistakes, especially the questions he often got wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 especially 是「尤其」（第 1 个义项：在同类中格外突出）；句意：考前复习时，他尤其重视错题，反复看那些容易出错的题。

senses.title: More than usual
senses.definition: more than usual or more than others
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或比其他人更突出
senses.example: The streets are busy, especially on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 街上很热闹，尤其是周末。
senses.why: The word marks one member of a group as standing out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把群体中的某一员标为格外突出。

senses.title: For a particular purpose
senses.definition: for one particular purpose rather than in general
senses.definitionCN: 为某个特定目的而非一般用途
senses.example: This tool is especially designed for small hands.
senses.exampleCN: 这件工具是专门为小手设计的。
senses.why: Singling out one purpose is another way of making something special.
senses.whyCN: 单独挑出一个目的，是让某事物特别的另一种方式。

intro.en: Especially is especial plus -ly, from Latin specialis, belonging to a kind.
intro.cn: especially 由 especial 加 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 specialis（属于某一类的）。

items.en: Species means a kind or appearance.
items.cn: species 意为种类或外观。

items.en: Specialis means belonging to a particular kind.
items.cn: specialis 意为属于特定种类的。

items.en: Especial enters French with the sense of special.
items.cn: especial 以「特别的」含义进入法语。

items.en: Especial means distinguished from others.
items.cn: especial 意为从其他事物中突出。

items.en: Especially marks a standout case or purpose.
items.cn: especially 标记突出的情况或目的。

note.en: Especially is close to particularly and specially.
note.cn: especially 与 particularly、specially 相近。

entries.definition: especially, in a way worth noticing

normalIntro.en: Especially puts a spotlight on one item in a group.
normalIntro.cn: especially 就像把聚光灯打在群体中的某一项上。

normal.en: Especially important means more important than the rest.
normal.cn: especially important 意为比其余的更重要的。

normal.en: Especially for children means mostly aimed at them.
normal.cn: especially for children 意为主要针对孩子。

normal.en: Not especially means only a little or not very.
normal.cn: not especially 意为并不太。

normal.en: The adjective is especial, though special is more common.
normal.cn: 形容词是 especial，不过 special 更常用。

normal.en: Compare specially: specially means for a purpose, especially means above all.
normal.cn: 对比 specially：specially 意为专门地，especially 意为尤其。

abstract.en: Picture one bright star in a dark sky.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗天空中一颗格外明亮的星。

abstract.en: Imagine one voice rising above a choir.
abstract.cn: 想象合唱中一个声音高过其他声音。

abstract.en: Think of a page with one word circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上有一个词被红笔圈出。

examples.en: I love fruit, especially peaches.
examples.cn: 我喜欢水果，尤其是桃子。

examples.en: The roads are dangerous, especially at night.
examples.cn: 这些路很危险，尤其是在夜里。

examples.en: This course is especially useful for beginners.
examples.cn: 这门课对初学者特别有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（外）＋ special（特别）＋ ly」——从普通中特别挑出来，就是尤其；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 species（种类）→ specialis（属于某类的）→ 古法语 especial → especial ＋ -ly → especially，核心义「从同类中格外突出」。

sensesIntro.en: Especially first marks something as more than usual, and then marks a special purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: especially 先把某事物标为格外突出，再标记特定目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one face lit by a spotlight in a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中一张被聚光灯照亮的脸。

branches.en: One member stands out above the rest.
branches.cn: 其中一员比其他成员更突出。

branches.en: The word can also mark a special purpose.
branches.cn: 这个词也能标记特殊目的。

branches.en: A standout item often serves a standout use.
branches.cn: 突出的东西往往有突出的用途。

branches.en: Emphasis is the main job of the word.
branches.cn: 强调是这个词的主要功能。

branches.en: A tool made for one job is especially designed.
branches.cn: 为一项工作特制的工具就是专门设计的。

intro.en: Especially adds the adverb ending -ly to especial, which shares a root with special.
intro.cn: especially 在 especial 后加副词词尾 -ly，而 especial 与 special 同根。

latinIntro.en: Latin species, a kind, gives specialis and the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species（种类）衍生出 specialis 及整个词族。

items.example: Species supplies the idea of a kind.
Specialis marks what belongs to a kind.
items.exampleCN: specialis 标记属于某类的事物。

items.example: Special is the common shorter form.
items.exampleCN: special 是常用的较短形式。

items.example: Specially marks purpose rather than degree.
items.exampleCN: specially 标记目的而非程度。

items.example: A specialist knows one field deeply.
items.exampleCN: specialist 深入掌握某一领域。

definition_en: a short piece of writing about a subject
core_image: 一叠写满字的纸，第一页写着标题和观点
scene: 老师让我们写一篇关于城市生活的短文，下周一交。The teacher asked us to write an essay about city life and hand it in next Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 essay 是「短文」（第 1 个义项：围绕一个主题写的短篇文章）；句意：老师让我们写一篇关于城市生活的短文，下周一交。

senses.title: A short piece of writing
senses.definition: a short piece of writing that gives the writer's ideas on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 就某一主题表达作者观点的短篇文章
senses.example: She wrote an essay on modern art.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一篇关于现代艺术的文章。
senses.why: The French source means an attempt, so an essay is an attempt to put ideas into words.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为尝试，因此文章就是把想法写成文字的尝试。

senses.title: An attempt
senses.definition: an attempt to do something, used in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的尝试，用于正式书面语
senses.example: His first essay in politics ended in failure.
senses.exampleCN: 他初次尝试政治以失败告终。
senses.why: The older sense of a trial attempt still appears in formal English.
senses.whyCN: 「尝试」这一古老含义仍出现在正式英语中。

intro.en: Essay comes from French essai, a trial, from Latin exigere, to weigh or test.
intro.cn: essay 源自法语 essai（尝试），源自拉丁语 exigere（称量、检验）。

items.en: Exigere means to weigh or examine.
items.cn: exigere 意为称量或检验。

items.en: Essai means a trial or attempt.
items.cn: essai 意为尝试或试验。

items.en: Montaigne's essays make the word famous.
items.cn: 蒙田的随笔让这个词广为人知。

items.en: Essay means a short written composition.
items.cn: essay 指短篇书面作品。

items.en: School essays are a common use.
items.cn: 学校作文是常见用法。

note.en: Essay is close to article and paper, but usually shorter and personal.
note.cn: essay 与文章、论文相近，但通常更短、更具个人色彩。

entries.definition: a test of metal or quality
a piece of writing in a newspaper
a long academic piece of writing
a piece of writing done as school work

normalIntro.en: An essay is an attempt with a pen: you try out your ideas on paper.
normalIntro.cn: essay 是一次用笔的尝试：在纸上试验自己的想法。

normal.en: Write an essay means produce a short paper.
normal.cn: write an essay 意为写一篇短文。

normal.en: An essay question asks for discussion, not a single word.
normal.cn: essay question 要求论述，而不是一个单词。

normal.en: An essay on a subject is written about it.
normal.cn: an essay on a subject 是就某主题写的文章。

normal.en: An essayist writes essays as a craft.
normal.cn: essayist 以写随笔为业。

normal.en: Compare article: an article is published, an essay may be for class.
normal.cn: 对比 article：article 多指发表的文章，essay 可以是为课堂写的。

abstract.en: Picture a blank page slowly filling with neat lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页白纸渐渐写满整齐的字行。

abstract.en: Imagine a title at the top and one clear idea below.
abstract.cn: 想象顶端一个标题，下面一个清晰的观点。

abstract.en: Think of a writer testing an idea like a small experiment.
abstract.cn: 想象作家像做小实验一样检验一个想法。

examples.en: He handed in his essay two days late.
examples.cn: 他晚了两天交文章。

examples.en: The essay won first prize in the contest.
examples.cn: 这篇文章在比赛中获得一等奖。

examples.en: Her essay on friendship is easy to read.
examples.cn: 她写友情的文章读起来很轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essay」听起来像「爱写」——爱写的人常写短文，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量、检验）→ 法语 essai（尝试）→ essay，核心义「对想法的文字试验」。

sensesIntro.en: Essay first means a short written work, and retains an older formal sense of an attempt.
sensesIntro.cn: essay 先指短篇文字作品，并保留「尝试」这一较古老的正式含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page filled with a title and a line of argument.
core.cn: 核心意象：写有标题与论点的一页纸。

branches.en: A short composition is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 短篇文章是日常义项。

branches.en: The old sense of an attempt survives in formal use.
branches.cn: 「尝试」的旧义在正式用法中保留。

branches.en: Writing an essay is an attempt to explain an idea.
branches.cn: 写文章就是尝试解释一个想法。

branches.en: School and exams make the word common.
branches.cn: 学校与考试让这个词十分常见。

branches.en: An essay has a subject, a view and a conclusion.
branches.cn: 文章有主题、观点与结论。

intro.en: Essay comes through French essai from Latin exigere, to weigh.
intro.cn: essay 经法语 essai 源自拉丁语 exigere（称量）。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere means to drive out, weigh or test.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 意为驱出、称量或检验。

items.example: Ex- appears in the Latin source.
items.exampleCN: ex- 出现在拉丁语来源中。

items.example: Agere is the second part of exigere.
items.exampleCN: agere 是 exigere 的后半部分。

items.example: French essai gives the English word.
items.exampleCN: 法语 essai 给出英语词形。

items.example: An essayist writes short prose pieces.
Essayistic describes a loose written style.
items.exampleCN: essayistic 描述自由的写作风格。

definition_zh: 必不可少的；本质的；要素
definition_en: completely necessary, or forming the basic nature of something
core_image: 一座桥最关键的那块基石，抽掉它整座桥就会塌
scene: 水对所有的生物都是必不可少的，没有它谁也活不了。Water is essential to all living things, and nothing can survive without it.
sceneCN: 这里 essential 是「必不可少的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就完全无法维持）；句意：水对所有的生物都是必不可少的，没有它谁也活不了。

senses.title: Completely necessary
senses.definition: so important that something cannot work without it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到没有它就无法运作
senses.example: Sleep is essential for good health.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠对健康必不可少。
senses.why: The word comes from essence, so what is essential belongs to the very being of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 essence，因此 essential 指属于事物存在本身的东西。

senses.title: Forming the basic nature
senses.definition: forming the central nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某事物的核心性质
senses.example: Freedom is an essential feature of democracy.
senses.exampleCN: 自由是民主的本质特征。
senses.why: The basic nature of a thing is what cannot be removed without changing it.
senses.whyCN: 事物的本质就是抽掉后它就不再是它自己的东西。

senses.title: A basic necessary thing
senses.definition: something that is completely necessary
senses.definitionCN: 完全不可缺少的事物
senses.example: The guide covers the essentials of camping.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南涵盖了露营的基本要点。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the necessary things themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指那些必要的事物本身。

intro.en: Essential comes from Late Latin essentialis, from essentia, being or nature.
intro.cn: essential 源自晚期拉丁语 essentialis，来自 essentia（存在、本性）。

items.en: Essentia means being or nature.
items.cn: essentia 意为存在或本性。

items.en: Essentialis means belonging to the essence.
items.cn: essentialis 意为属于本质的。

items.en: Essential means forming the nature of something.
items.cn: essential 意为构成某事物的本性。

items.en: It also means absolutely necessary.
items.cn: 它也意为绝对必要。

items.en: The plural essentials names necessary items.
items.cn: 复数 essentials 指必需物品。

note.en: Essential is close to necessary and vital, and to essence in meaning.
note.cn: essential 与必要的、至关重要的相近，并与 essence 意义相连。

entries.definition: extremely important for life or success

normalIntro.en: Essential is about essence: remove it and the thing loses itself.
normalIntro.cn: essential 关乎 essence：抽掉它，事物就不再是自己。

normal.en: Essential to health means health fails without it.
normal.cn: essential to health 意为没有它健康就会垮。

normal.en: An essential part is one you cannot remove.
normal.cn: an essential part 是你不能去掉的部分。

normal.en: Absolutely essential means there is no substitute.
normal.cn: absolutely essential 意为没有替代品。

normal.en: The bare essentials are the smallest necessary set.
normal.cn: the bare essentials 是最低限度的必需品。

normal.en: Compare vital: vital stresses life, essential stresses necessity.
normal.cn: 对比 vital：vital 强调生命，essential 强调必要。

abstract.en: Picture the one stone that holds up an arch.
abstract.cn: 想象支撑整座拱门的那块石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a recipe missing its key ingredient.
abstract.cn: 想象一份缺少关键原料的食谱。

abstract.en: Think of a key that opens the only door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能打开唯一那扇门的钥匙。

examples.en: It is essential to book early.
examples.cn: 尽早预订是必不可少的。

examples.en: Trust is an essential part of friendship.
examples.cn: 信任是友谊的关键部分。

examples.en: Pack only the essentials for the trip.
examples.cn: 旅行只带必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essence（本质）＋ ial」——属于本质的东西，就是必不可少的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 essentia（存在、本性）→ 晚期拉丁语 essentialis → essential，核心义「属于事物本性、缺之不可」。

sensesIntro.en: Essential first means completely necessary, then belonging to the basic nature, and as a noun it names necessary things.
sensesIntro.cn: essential 先指完全必要，再指属于本质，作名词时指必需品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the keystone whose removal collapses the arch.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽掉就会让拱门倒塌的拱心石。

branches.en: Complete necessity is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 完全必要是日常义项。

branches.en: The basic nature of a thing is its essence.
branches.cn: 事物的基本性质就是它的本质。

branches.en: As a noun it names necessary items.
branches.cn: 作名词时指必需物品。

branches.en: What belongs to the essence is what cannot be removed.
branches.cn: 属于本质的东西就是不能抽掉的东西。

branches.en: The essentials of a subject are its core points.
branches.cn: 一门学科的 essentials 就是其核心要点。

intro.en: Essential adds -ial to essence, from Latin essentia.
intro.cn: essential 在 essence 上加 -ial，源自拉丁语 essentia。

latinIntro.en: Essentia comes from esse, to be, so essence is the very being of a thing.
latinIntro.cn: essentia 来自 esse（存在），因此本质就是事物的存在本身。

items.example: Esse is the verb of being.
items.exampleCN: esse 是表示存在的动词。

items.example: Essential describes what cannot be removed.
items.exampleCN: essential 描述不能去掉的东西。
